verses.28: That is the thing which I spoke to Pharaoh. What God is about to do he has shown to Pharaoh.
verses.29: Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.30: There will arise after them seven years of famine, and all the plenty will be forgotten in the land of Egypt. The famine will consume the land,
verses.31: and the plenty will not be known in the land by reason of that famine which follows; for it will be very grievous.
verses.32: The dream was doubled to Pharaoh, because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.
verses.33: “Now therefore let Pharaoh look for a discreet and wise man, and set him over the land of Egypt.
verses.34: Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint overseers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt’s produce in the seven plenteous years.
verses.35: Let them gather all the food of these good years that come, and lay up grain under the hand of Pharaoh for food in the cities, and let them keep it.
verses.36: The food will be for a store to the land against the seven years of famine, which will be in the land of Egypt; that the land not perish through the famine.”
verses.37: The thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
verses.38: Pharaoh said to his servants, “Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom is the Spirit of God?”
verses.39: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Because God has shown you all of this, there is no one so discreet and wise as you.
verses.40: You shall be over my house, and according to your word will all my people be ruled. Only in the throne I will be greater than you.”
verses.41: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Behold, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.”
verses.42: Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck,
verses.43: and he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had. They cried before him, “Bow the knee!” He set him over all the land of Egypt.
verses.44: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh, and without you shall no man lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.”
verses.45: Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphenath-Paneah; and he gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On as a wife. Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.
verses.46: Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.47: In the seven plenteous years the earth produced abundantly.
verses.48: He gathered up all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities: the food of the field, which was around every city, he laid up in the same.
verses.49: Joseph laid up grain as the sand of the sea, very much, until he stopped counting, for it was without number.
verses.50: To Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, bore to him.
verses.51: Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, “For”, he said, “God has made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.”
verses.52: The name of the second, he called Ephraim: “For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”
verses.53: The seven years of plenty, that were in the land of Egypt, came to an end.
verses.54: The seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
verses.55: When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do.”
verses.56: The famine was over all the surface of the earth. Joseph opened all the store houses, and sold to the Egyptians. The famine was severe in the land of Egypt.
verses.57: All countries came into Egypt, to Joseph, to buy grain, because the famine was severe in all the earth.

verses.1: Now Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, “Why do you look at one another?”
verses.2: He said, “Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there, and buy for us from there, so that we may live, and not die.”
verses.3: Joseph’s ten brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
verses.4: But Jacob didn’t send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, with his brothers; for he said, “Lest perhaps harm happen to him.”
verses.5: The sons of Israel came to buy among those who came, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
verses.6: Joseph was the governor over the land. It was he who sold to all the people of the land. Joseph’s brothers came, and bowed themselves down to him with their faces to the earth.
verses.7:
Joseph saw his brothers, and he recognized them, but acted like a stranger to them, and spoke roughly with them. He said to them, “Where did you come from?”
They said, “From the land of Canaan to buy food.”
verses.8: Joseph recognized his brothers, but they didn’t recognize him.
verses.9: Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed about them, and said to them, “You are spies! You have come to see the nakedness of the land.”
verses.10: They said to him, “No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.
verses.11: We are all one man’s sons; we are honest men. Your servants are not spies.”
verses.12: He said to them, “No, but you have come to see the nakedness of the land!”
verses.13: They said, “We, your servants, are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is today with our father, and one is no more.”
verses.14: Joseph said to them, “It is like I told you, saying, ‘You are spies!’
verses.15: By this you shall be tested. By the life of Pharaoh, you shall not go out from here, unless your youngest brother comes here.
verses.16: Send one of you, and let him get your brother, and you shall be bound, that your words may be tested, whether there is truth in you, or else by the life of Pharaoh surely you are spies.”
verses.17: He put them all together into custody for three days.
verses.18: Joseph said to them the third day, “Do this, and live, for I fear God.
verses.19: If you are honest men, then let one of your brothers be bound in your prison; but you go, carry grain for the famine of your houses.
verses.20:
Bring your youngest brother to me; so will your words be verified, and you won’t die.”
They did so.
verses.21: They said to one another, “We are certainly guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul, when he begged us, and we wouldn’t listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us.”
verses.22: Reuben answered them, saying, “Didn’t I tell you, saying, ‘Don’t sin against the child,’ and you wouldn’t listen? Therefore also, behold, his blood is required.”
verses.23: They didn’t know that Joseph understood them; for there was an interpreter between them.
verses.24: He turned himself away from them, and wept. Then he returned to them, and spoke to them, and took Simeon from among them, and bound him before their eyes.
verses.25: Then Joseph gave a command to fill their bags with grain, and to restore each man’s money into his sack, and to give them food for the way. So it was done to them.
verses.26: They loaded their donkeys with their grain, and departed from there.
verses.27: As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey food in the lodging place, he saw his money. Behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.
verses.28: He said to his brothers, “My money is restored! Behold, it is in my sack!” Their hearts failed them, and they turned trembling to one another, saying, “What is this that God has done to us?”
verses.29: They came to Jacob their father, to the land of Canaan, and told him all that had happened to them, saying,
verses.30: “The man, the lord of the land, spoke roughly with us, and took us for spies of the country.
verses.31: We said to him, ‘We are honest men. We are no spies.
verses.32: We are twelve brothers, sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is today with our father in the land of Canaan.’
verses.33: The man, the lord of the land, said to us, ‘By this I will know that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me, and take grain for the famine of your houses, and go your way.
verses.34: Bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will know that you are not spies, but that you are honest men. So I will deliver your brother to you, and you shall trade in the land.’”
verses.35: As they emptied their sacks, behold, each man’s bundle of money was in his sack. When they and their father saw their bundles of money, they were afraid.
verses.36: Jacob, their father, said to them, “You have bereaved me of my children! Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you want to take Benjamin away. All these things are against me.”
verses.37: Reuben spoke to his father, saying, “Kill my two sons, if I don’t bring him to you. Entrust him to my care, and I will bring him to you again.”
verses.38: He said, “My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he only is left. If harm happens to him along the way in which you go, then you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.”

verses.1: The famine was severe in the land.
verses.2: When they had eaten up the grain which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said to them, “Go again, buy us a little more food.”
verses.3: Judah spoke to him, saying, “The man solemnly warned us, saying, ‘You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.’
verses.4: If you’ll send our brother with us, we’ll go down and buy you food,
verses.5: but if you’ll not send him, we’ll not go down, for the man said to us, ‘You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.’”
verses.6: Israel said, “Why did you treat me so badly, telling the man that you had another brother?”
verses.7: They said, “The man asked directly concerning ourselves, and concerning our relatives, saying, ‘Is your father still alive? Have you another brother?’ We just answered his questions. Is there any way we could know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother down?’”
verses.8: Judah said to Israel, his father, “Send the boy with me, and we’ll get up and go, so that we may live, and not die, both we, and you, and also our little ones.
verses.9: I’ll be collateral for him. From my hand will you require him. If I don’t bring him to you, and set him before you, then let me bear the blame forever,
verses.10: for if we hadn’t delayed, surely we would have returned a second time by now.”
verses.11: Their father, Israel, said to them, “If it must be so, then do this. Take from the choice fruits of the land in your bags, and carry down a present for the man, a little balm, a little honey, spices and myrrh, nuts, and almonds;
verses.12: and take double money in your hand, and take back the money that was returned in the mouth of your sacks. Perhaps it was an oversight.
verses.13: Take your brother also, get up, and return to the man.
verses.14: May God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin. If I am bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.”
verses.15: The men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and got up, went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
verses.16: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, “Bring the men into the house, and butcher an animal, and prepare; for the men will dine with me at noon.”
verses.17: The man did as Joseph commanded, and the man brought the men to Joseph’s house.
verses.18: The men were afraid, because they were brought to Joseph’s house; and they said, “Because of the money that was returned in our sacks the first time, we’re brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, attack us, and seize us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”
verses.19: They came near to the steward of Joseph’s house, and they spoke to him at the door of the house,
verses.20: and said, “Oh, my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food.
verses.21: When we came to the lodging place, we opened our sacks, and behold, each man’s money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight. We have brought it back in our hand.
verses.22: We have brought down other money in our hand to buy food. We don’t know who put our money in our sacks.”
verses.23: He said, “Peace be to you. Don’t be afraid. Your God, and the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks. I received your money.” He brought Simeon out to them.
verses.24: The man brought the men into Joseph’s house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet. He gave their donkeys fodder.
verses.25: They prepared the present for Joseph’s coming at noon, for they heard that they should eat bread there.
verses.26: When Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves down to the earth before him.
verses.27: He asked them of their welfare, and said, “Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he yet alive?”
verses.28: They said, “Your servant, our father, is well. He is still alive.” They bowed down humbly.
verses.29: He lifted up his eyes, and saw Benjamin, his brother, his mother’s son, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” He said, “God be gracious to you, my son.”
verses.30: Joseph hurried, for his heart yearned over his brother; and he sought a place to weep. He entered into his room, and wept there.
verses.31: He washed his face, and came out. He controlled himself, and said, “Serve the meal.”
verses.32: They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians, that ate with him, by themselves, because the Egyptians don’t eat bread with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.
verses.33: They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth, and the men marveled one with another.
verses.34: He sent portions to them from before him, but Benjamin’s portion was five times as much as any of theirs. They drank, and were merry with him.

verses.1: He commanded the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s money in his sack’s mouth.
verses.2: Put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, with his grain money.” He did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
verses.3: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.
verses.4: When they had gone out of the city, and were not yet far off, Joseph said to his steward, “Up, follow after the men. When you overtake them, ask them, ‘Why have you rewarded evil for good?
verses.5: Isn’t this that from which my lord drinks, and by which he indeed divines? You have done evil in so doing.’”
verses.6: He overtook them, and he spoke these words to them.
verses.7: They said to him, “Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants that they should do such a thing!
verses.8: Behold, the money, which we found in our sacks’ mouths, we brought again to you out of the land of Canaan. How then should we steal silver or gold out of your lord’s house?
verses.9: With whomever of your servants it is found, let him die, and we also will be my lord’s slaves.”
verses.10: He said, “Now also let it be according to your words: he with whom it is found will be my slave; and you will be blameless.”
verses.11: Then they hurried, and each man took his sack down to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
verses.12: He searched, beginning with the oldest, and ending at the youngest. The cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.
verses.13: Then they tore their clothes, and each man loaded his donkey, and returned to the city.
verses.14: Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house, and he was still there. They fell on the ground before him.
verses.15: Joseph said to them, “What deed is this that you have done? Don’t you know that such a man as I can indeed divine?”
verses.16: Judah said, “What will we tell my lord? What will we speak? Or how will we clear ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of your servants. Behold, we are my lord’s slaves, both we, and he also in whose hand the cup is found.”
verses.17: He said, “Far be it from me that I should do so. The man in whose hand the cup is found, he will be my slave; but as for you, go up in peace to your father.”
verses.18: Then Judah came near to him, and said, “Oh, my lord, please let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and don’t let your anger burn against your servant; for you are even as Pharaoh.
verses.19: My lord asked his servants, saying, ‘Have you a father, or a brother?’
verses.20: We said to my lord, ‘We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother; and his father loves him.’
verses.21: You said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes on him.’
verses.22: We said to my lord, ‘The boy can’t leave his father: for if he should leave his father, his father would die.’
verses.23: You said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will see my face no more.’
verses.24: When we came up to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
verses.25: Our father said, ‘Go again and buy us a little food.’
verses.26: We said, ‘We can’t go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down: for we may not see the man’s face, unless our youngest brother is with us.’
verses.27: Your servant, my father, said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons:
verses.28: and the one went out from me, and I said, “Surely he is torn in pieces”; and I haven’t seen him since.
verses.29: If you take this one also from me, and harm happens to him, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.’
verses.30: Now therefore when I come to your servant my father, and the boy is not with us; since his life is bound up in the boy’s life;
verses.31: it will happen, when he sees that the boy is no more, that he will die. Your servants will bring down the gray hairs of your servant, our father, with sorrow to Sheol.
verses.32: For your servant became collateral for the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I don’t bring him to you, then I will bear the blame to my father forever.’
verses.33: Now therefore, please let your servant stay instead of the boy, my lord’s slave; and let the boy go up with his brothers.
verses.34: For how will I go up to my father, if the boy isn’t with me?—lest I see the evil that will come on my father.”

verses.1: Then Joseph couldn’t control himself before all those who stood before him, and he cried, “Cause everyone to go out from me!” No one else stood with him, while Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
verses.2: He wept aloud. The Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.
verses.3:
Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Does my father still live?”
His brothers couldn’t answer him; for they were terrified at his presence.
verses.4:
Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.”
They came near. “He said, I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
verses.5: Now don’t be grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
verses.6: For these two years the famine has been in the land, and there are yet five years, in which there will be no plowing and no harvest.
verses.7: God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant in the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.
verses.8: So now it wasn’t you who sent me here, but God, and he has made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
verses.9: Hurry, and go up to my father, and tell him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says, “God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me. Don’t wait.
verses.10: You shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you will be near to me, you, your children, your children’s children, your flocks, your herds, and all that you have.
verses.11: There I will nourish you; for there are yet five years of famine; lest you come to poverty, you, and your household, and all that you have.”’
verses.12: Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.
verses.13: You shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. You shall hurry and bring my father down here.”
verses.14: He fell on his brother Benjamin’s neck, and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
verses.15: He kissed all his brothers, and wept on them. After that his brothers talked with him.
verses.16: The report of it was heard in Pharaoh’s house, saying, “Joseph’s brothers have come.” It pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.
verses.17: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Do this. Load your animals, and go, travel to the land of Canaan.
verses.18: Take your father and your households, and come to me, and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.’
verses.19: Now you are commanded: do this. Take wagons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.
verses.20: Also, don’t concern yourselves about your belongings, for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.”
verses.21: The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.
verses.22: He gave each one of them changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.
verses.23: He sent the following to his father: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provision for his father by the way.
verses.24: So he sent his brothers away, and they departed. He said to them, “See that you don’t quarrel on the way.”
verses.25: They went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.
verses.26: They told him, saying, “Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.” His heart fainted, for he didn’t believe them.
verses.27: They told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them. When he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob, their father, revived.
verses.28: Israel said, “It is enough. Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”

verses.1: Israel traveled with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father, Isaac.
verses.2:
God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and said, “Jacob, Jacob!”
He said, “Here I am.”
verses.3: He said, “I am God, the God of your father. Don’t be afraid to go down into Egypt, for there I will make of you a great nation.
verses.4: I will go down with you into Egypt. I will also surely bring you up again. Joseph will close your eyes.”
verses.5: Jacob rose up from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried Jacob, their father, their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
verses.6: They took their livestock, and their goods, which they had gotten in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt—Jacob, and all his offspring with him,
verses.7: his sons, and his sons’ sons with him, his daughters, and his sons’ daughters, and he brought all his offspring with him into Egypt.
verses.8: These are the names of the children of Israel, who came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.
verses.9: The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
verses.10: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman.
verses.11: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
verses.12: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
verses.13: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron.
verses.14: The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
verses.15: These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan Aram, with his daughter Dinah. All the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty-three.
verses.16: The sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
verses.17: The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and Serah their sister. The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
verses.18: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob, even sixteen souls.
verses.19: The sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife: Joseph and Benjamin.
verses.20: To Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.
verses.21: The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
verses.22: These are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob: all the souls were fourteen.
verses.23: The son of Dan: Hushim.
verses.24: The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
verses.25: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob: all the souls were seven.
verses.26: All the souls who came with Jacob into Egypt, who were his direct offspring, besides Jacob’s sons’ wives, all the souls were sixty-six.
verses.27: The sons of Joseph, who were born to him in Egypt, were two souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob, who came into Egypt, were seventy.
verses.28: He sent Judah before him to Joseph, to show the way before him to Goshen, and they came into the land of Goshen.
verses.29: Joseph prepared his chariot, and went up to meet Israel, his father, in Goshen. He presented himself to him, and fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.
verses.30: Israel said to Joseph, “Now let me die, since I have seen your face, that you are still alive.”
verses.31: Joseph said to his brothers, and to his father’s house, “I will go up, and speak with Pharaoh, and will tell him, ‘My brothers, and my father’s house, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.
verses.32: These men are shepherds, for they have been keepers of livestock, and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.’
verses.33: It will happen, when Pharaoh summons you, and will say, ‘What is your occupation?’
verses.34: that you shall say, ‘Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth even until now, both we, and our fathers:’ that you may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.”

verses.1: Then Joseph went in and told Pharaoh, and said, “My father and my brothers, with their flocks, their herds, and all that they own, have come out of the land of Canaan; and behold, they are in the land of Goshen.”
verses.2: From among his brothers he took five men, and presented them to Pharaoh.
verses.3:
Pharaoh said to his brothers, “What is your occupation?”
They said to Pharaoh, “Your servants are shepherds, both we, and our fathers.”
verses.4: They said to Pharaoh, “We have come to live as foreigners in the land, for there is no pasture for your servants’ flocks. For the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. Now therefore, please let your servants dwell in the land of Goshen.”
verses.5: Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, “Your father and your brothers have come to you.
verses.6: The land of Egypt is before you. Make your father and your brothers dwell in the best of the land. Let them dwell in the land of Goshen. If you know any able men among them, then put them in charge of my livestock.”
verses.7: Joseph brought in Jacob, his father, and set him before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
verses.8: Pharaoh said to Jacob, “How many are the days of the years of your life?”
verses.9: Jacob said to Pharaoh, “The days of the years of my pilgrimage are one hundred thirty years. Few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not attained to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.”
verses.10: Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from the presence of Pharaoh.
verses.11: Joseph placed his father and his brothers, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
verses.12: Joseph nourished his father, his brothers, and all of his father’s household, with bread, according to their families.
verses.13: There was no bread in all the land; for the famine was very severe, so that the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan fainted by reason of the famine.
verses.14: Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the grain which they bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh’s house.
verses.15: When the money was all spent in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph, and said, “Give us bread, for why should we die in your presence? For our money fails.”
verses.16: Joseph said, “Give me your livestock; and I will give you food for your livestock, if your money is gone.”
verses.17: They brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses, and for the flocks, and for the herds, and for the donkeys: and he fed them with bread in exchange for all their livestock for that year.
verses.18: When that year was ended, they came to him the second year, and said to him, “We will not hide from my lord how our money is all spent, and the herds of livestock are my lord’s. There is nothing left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands.
verses.19: Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh. Give us seed, that we may live, and not die, and that the land won’t be desolate.”
verses.20: So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, for every man of the Egyptians sold his field, because the famine was severe on them, and the land became Pharaoh’s.
verses.21: As for the people, he moved them to the cities from one end of the border of Egypt even to the other end of it.
verses.22: Only he didn’t buy the land of the priests, for the priests had a portion from Pharaoh, and ate their portion which Pharaoh gave them. That is why they didn’t sell their land.
verses.23: Then Joseph said to the people, “Behold, I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh. Behold, here is seed for you, and you shall sow the land.
verses.24: It will happen at the harvests, that you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four parts will be your own, for seed of the field, for your food, for them of your households, and for food for your little ones.”
verses.25: They said, “You have saved our lives! Let us find favor in the sight of my lord, and we will be Pharaoh’s servants.”
verses.26: Joseph made it a statute concerning the land of Egypt to this day, that Pharaoh should have the fifth. Only the land of the priests alone didn’t become Pharaoh’s.
verses.27: Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; and they got themselves possessions therein, and were fruitful, and multiplied exceedingly.
verses.28: Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years. So the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were one hundred forty-seven years.
verses.29: The time came near that Israel must die, and he called his son Joseph, and said to him, “If now I have found favor in your sight, please put your hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly with me. Please don’t bury me in Egypt,
verses.30:
but when I sleep with my fathers, you shall carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their burying place.”
He said, “I will do as you have said.”
verses.31: He said, “Swear to me,” and he swore to him. Israel bowed himself on the bed’s head.

verses.1: After these things, someone said to Joseph, “Behold, your father is sick.” He took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
verses.2: Someone told Jacob, and said, “Behold, your son Joseph comes to you,” and Israel strengthened himself, and sat on the bed.
verses.3: Jacob said to Joseph, “God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,
verses.4: and said to me, ‘Behold, I will make you fruitful, and multiply you, and I will make of you a company of peoples, and will give this land to your offspring after you for an everlasting possession.’
verses.5: Now your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you into Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh, even as Reuben and Simeon, will be mine.
verses.6: Your issue, whom you become the father of after them, will be yours. They will be called after the name of their brothers in their inheritance.
verses.7: As for me, when I came from Paddan, Rachel died by me in the land of Canaan on the way, when there was still some distance to come to Ephrath, and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath (also called Bethlehem).”
verses.8: Israel saw Joseph’s sons, and said, “Who are these?”
verses.9:
Joseph said to his father, “They are my sons, whom God has given me here.”
He said, “Please bring them to me, and I will bless them.”
verses.10: Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he couldn’t see. He brought them near to him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.
verses.11: Israel said to Joseph, “I didn’t think I would see your face, and behold, God has let me see your offspring also.”
verses.12: Joseph brought them out from between his knees, and he bowed himself with his face to the earth.
verses.13: Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel’s right hand, and brought them near to him.
verses.14: Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it on Ephraim’s head, who was the younger, and his left hand on Manasseh’s head, guiding his hands knowingly, for Manasseh was the firstborn.
verses.15: He blessed Joseph, and said, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has fed me all my life long to this day,
verses.16: the angel who has redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads, and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac. Let them grow into a multitude upon the earth.”
verses.17: When Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand on the head of Ephraim, it displeased him. He held up his father’s hand, to remove it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s head.
verses.18: Joseph said to his father, “Not so, my father; for this is the firstborn; put your right hand on his head.”
verses.19: His father refused, and said, “I know, my son, I know. He also will become a people, and he also will be great. However, his younger brother will be greater than he, and his offspring will become a multitude of nations.”
verses.20: He blessed them that day, saying, “In you will Israel bless, saying, ‘God make you as Ephraim and as Manasseh’” He set Ephraim before Manasseh.
verses.21: Israel said to Joseph, “Behold, I am dying, but God will be with you, and bring you again to the land of your fathers.
verses.22: Moreover I have given to you one portion above your brothers, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.”

verses.1: Jacob called to his sons, and said: “Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which will happen to you in the days to come.
verses.2:
Assemble yourselves, and hear, you sons of Jacob.
Listen to Israel, your father.
verses.3:
“Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength;
excelling in dignity, and excelling in power.
verses.5:
“Simeon and Levi are brothers.
Their swords are weapons of violence.
verses.6:
My soul, don’t come into their council.
My glory, don’t be united to their assembly;
for in their anger they killed men.
In their self-will they hamstrung cattle.
verses.7:
Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce;
and their wrath, for it was cruel.
I will divide them in Jacob,
and scatter them in Israel.
verses.8:
“Judah, your brothers will praise you.
Your hand will be on the neck of your enemies.
Your father’s sons will bow down before you.
verses.9:
Judah is a lion’s cub.
From the prey, my son, you have gone up.
He stooped down, he crouched as a lion,
as a lioness.
Who will rouse him up?
verses.10:
The scepter will not depart from Judah,
nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet,
until he comes to whom it belongs.
To him will the obedience of the peoples be.
verses.11:
Binding his foal to the vine,
his donkey’s colt to the choice vine;
he has washed his garments in wine,
his robes in the blood of grapes.
verses.12:
His eyes will be red with wine,
his teeth white with milk.
verses.13:
“Zebulun will dwell at the haven of the sea.
He will be for a haven of ships.
His border will be on Sidon.
verses.14:
“Issachar is a strong donkey,
lying down between the saddlebags.
verses.15:
He saw a resting place, that it was good,
the land, that it was pleasant.
He bows his shoulder to the burden,
and becomes a servant doing forced labor.
verses.16:
“Dan will judge his people,
as one of the tribes of Israel.
verses.17:
Dan will be a serpent on the trail,
an adder in the path,
That bites the horse’s heels,
so that his rider falls backward.
verses.18: I have waited for your salvation, Yahweh.
verses.19:
“A troop will press on Gad,
but he will press on their heel.
verses.20:
“Asher’s food will be rich.
He will produce royal dainties.
verses.21:
“Naphtali is a doe set free,
who bears beautiful fawns.
verses.22:
“Joseph is a fruitful vine,
a fruitful vine by a spring.
His branches run over the wall.
verses.23:
The archers have severely grieved him,
shot at him, and persecuted him:
verses.24:
But his bow remained strong.
The arms of his hands were made strong,
by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob,
(from there is the shepherd, the stone of Israel),
verses.25:
even by the God of your father, who will help you;
by the Almighty, who will bless you,
with blessings of heaven above,
blessings of the deep that lies below,
blessings of the breasts, and of the womb.
verses.26:
The blessings of your father have prevailed above the blessings of your ancestors,
above the boundaries of the ancient hills.
They will be on the head of Joseph,
on the crown of the head of him who is separated from his brothers.
verses.27:
“Benjamin is a ravenous wolf.
In the morning he will devour the prey.
At evening he will divide the plunder.”
verses.28: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father spoke to them and blessed them. He blessed everyone according to his blessing.
verses.29: He instructed them, and said to them, “I am to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
verses.30: in the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is before Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field from Ephron the Hittite as a burial place.
verses.31: There they buried Abraham and Sarah, his wife. There they buried Isaac and Rebekah, his wife, and there I buried Leah:
verses.32: the field and the cave that is therein, which was purchased from the children of Heth.”
verses.33: When Jacob finished charging his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the spirit, and was gathered to his people.

verses.1: Joseph fell on his father’s face, wept on him, and kissed him.
verses.2: Joseph commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father; and the physicians embalmed Israel.
verses.3: Forty days were fulfilled for him, for that is how many the days it takes to embalm. The Egyptians wept for him for seventy days.
verses.4: When the days of weeping for him were past, Joseph spoke to the house of Pharaoh, saying, “If now I have found favor in your eyes, please speak in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,
verses.5: ‘My father made me swear, saying, “Behold, I am dying. Bury me in my grave which I have dug for myself in the land of Canaan.” Now therefore, please let me go up and bury my father, and I will come again.’”
verses.6: Pharaoh said, “Go up, and bury your father, just like he made you swear.”
verses.7: Joseph went up to bury his father; and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, all the elders of the land of Egypt,
verses.8: All the house of Joseph, his brothers, and his father’s house. Only their little ones, their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen.
verses.9: There went up with him both chariots and horsemen. It was a very great company.
verses.10: They came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and there they lamented with a very great and severe lamentation. He mourned for his father seven days.
verses.11: When the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, “This is a grievous mourning by the Egyptians.” Therefore its name was called Abel Mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan.
verses.12: His sons did to him just as he commanded them,
verses.13: for his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field, as a possession for a burial site, from Ephron the Hittite, near Mamre.
verses.14: Joseph returned into Egypt—he, and his brothers, and all that went up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.
verses.15: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, “It may be that Joseph will hate us, and will fully pay us back for all the evil which we did to him.”
verses.16: They sent a message to Joseph, saying, “Your father commanded before he died, saying,
verses.17: ‘You shall tell Joseph, “Now please forgive the disobedience of your brothers, and their sin, because they did evil to you.”’ Now, please forgive the disobedience of the servants of the God of your father.” Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
verses.18: His brothers also went and fell down before his face; and they said, “Behold, we are your servants.”
verses.19: Joseph said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for am I in the place of God?
verses.20: As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is today, to save many people alive.
verses.21: Now therefore don’t be afraid. I will nourish you and your little ones.” He comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.
verses.22: Joseph lived in Egypt, he, and his father’s house. Joseph lived one hundred ten years.
verses.23: Joseph saw Ephraim’s children to the third generation. The children also of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born on Joseph’s knees.
verses.24: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am dying, but God will surely visit you, and bring you up out of this land to the land which he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”
verses.25: Joseph took an oath from the children of Israel, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here.”
verses.26: So Joseph died, being one hundred ten years old, and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

verses.1: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt (every man and his household came with Jacob):
verses.2: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,
verses.3: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,
verses.4: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
verses.5: All the souls who came out of Jacob’s body were seventy souls, and Joseph was in Egypt already.
verses.6: Joseph died, as did all his brothers, and all that generation.
verses.7: The children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and grew exceedingly mighty; and the land was filled with them.
verses.8: Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who didn’t know Joseph.
verses.9: He said to his people, “Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we.
verses.10: Come, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it happen that when any war breaks out, they also join themselves to our enemies, and fight against us, and escape out of the land.”
verses.11: Therefore they set taskmasters over them to afflict them with their burdens. They built storage cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Raamses.
verses.12: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and the more they spread out. They were grieved because of the children of Israel.
verses.13: The Egyptians ruthlessly made the children of Israel serve,
verses.14: and they made their lives bitter with hard service, in mortar and in brick, and in all kinds of service in the field, all their service, in which they ruthlessly made them serve.
verses.15: The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah,
verses.16: and he said, “When you perform the duty of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them on the birth stool; if it is a son, then you shall kill him; but if it is a daughter, then she shall live.”
verses.17: But the midwives feared God, and didn’t do what the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the baby boys alive.
verses.18: The king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said to them, “Why have you done this thing, and have saved the boys alive?”
verses.19: The midwives said to Pharaoh, “Because the Hebrew women aren’t like the Egyptian women; for they are vigorous, and give birth before the midwife comes to them.”
verses.20: God dealt well with the midwives, and the people multiplied, and grew very mighty.
verses.21: Because the midwives feared God, he gave them families.
verses.22: Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, “You shall cast every son who is born into the river, and every daughter you shall save alive.”

verses.1: A man of the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi as his wife.
verses.2: The woman conceived, and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.
verses.3: When she could no longer hide him, she took a papyrus basket for him, and coated it with tar and with pitch. She put the child in it, and laid it in the reeds by the river’s bank.
verses.4: His sister stood far off, to see what would be done to him.
verses.5: Pharaoh’s daughter came down to bathe at the river. Her maidens walked along by the riverside. She saw the basket among the reeds, and sent her servant to get it.
verses.6: She opened it, and saw the child, and behold, the baby cried. She had compassion on him, and said, “This is one of the Hebrews’ children.”
verses.7: Then his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Should I go and call a nurse for you from the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for you?”
verses.8:
Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Go.”
The young woman went and called the child’s mother.
verses.9:
Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this child away, and nurse him for me, and I will give you your wages.”
The woman took the child, and nursed it.
verses.10: The child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, and said, “Because I drew him out of the water.”
verses.11: In those days, when Moses had grown up, he went out to his brothers, and looked at their burdens. He saw an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, one of his brothers.
verses.12: He looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no one, he killed the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
verses.13: He went out the second day, and behold, two men of the Hebrews were fighting with each other. He said to him who did the wrong, “Why do you strike your fellow?”
verses.14:
He said, “Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you plan to kill me, as you killed the Egyptian?”
Moses was afraid, and said, “Surely this thing is known.”
verses.15: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and lived in the land of Midian, and he sat down by a well.
verses.16: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters. They came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.
verses.17: The shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.
verses.18: When they came to Reuel, their father, he said, “How is it that you have returned so early today?”
verses.19: They said, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and moreover he drew water for us, and watered the flock.”
verses.20: He said to his daughters, “Where is he? Why is it that you have left the man? Call him, that he may eat bread.”
verses.21: Moses was content to dwell with the man. He gave Moses Zipporah, his daughter.
verses.22: She bore a son, and he named him Gershom, for he said, “I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign land.”
verses.23: In the course of those many days, the king of Egypt died, and the children of Israel sighed because of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up to God because of the bondage.
verses.24: God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
verses.25: God saw the children of Israel, and God was concerned about them.

verses.1: Now Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro, his father-in-law, the priest of Midian, and he led the flock to the back of the wilderness, and came to God’s mountain, to Horeb.
verses.2: Yahweh’s angel appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the middle of a bush. He looked, and behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
verses.3: Moses said, “I will go now, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burned.”
verses.4:
When Yahweh saw that he came over to see, God called to him out of the middle of the bush, and said, “Moses! Moses!”
He said, “Here I am.”
verses.5: He said, “Don’t come close. Take off your sandals, for the place you are standing on is holy ground.”
verses.6:
Moreover he said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.”
Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look at God.
verses.7: Yahweh said, “I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters, for I know their sorrows.
verses.8: I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land to a good and large land, to a land flowing with milk and honey; to the place of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
verses.9: Now, behold, the cry of the children of Israel has come to me. Moreover I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them.
verses.10: Come now therefore, and I will send you to Pharaoh, that you may bring my people, the children of Israel, out of Egypt.”
verses.11: Moses said to God, “Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring the children of Israel out of Egypt?”
verses.12: He said, “Certainly I will be with you. This will be the token to you, that I have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God on this mountain.”
verses.13: Moses said to God, “Behold, when I come to the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you;’ and they ask me, ‘What is his name?’ What should I tell them?”
verses.14: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM,” and he said, “You shall tell the children of Israel this: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
verses.15: God said moreover to Moses, “You shall tell the children of Israel this, ‘Yahweh, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is my name forever, and this is my memorial to all generations.
verses.16: Go and gather the elders of Israel together, and tell them, ‘Yahweh, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, has appeared to me, saying, “I have surely visited you, and seen that which is done to you in Egypt;
verses.17: and I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt to the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, to a land flowing with milk and honey.”’
verses.18: They will listen to your voice, and you shall come, you and the elders of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and you shall tell him, ‘Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. Now please let us go three days’ journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to Yahweh, our God.’
verses.19: I know that the king of Egypt won’t give you permission to go, no, not by a mighty hand.
verses.20: I will reach out my hand and strike Egypt with all my wonders which I will do among them, and after that he will let you go.
verses.21: I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, and it will happen that when you go, you shall not go empty-handed.
verses.22: But every woman shall ask of her neighbor, and of her who visits her house, jewels of silver, jewels of gold, and clothing; and you shall put them on your sons, and on your daughters. You shall plunder the Egyptians.”

verses.1: Moses answered, “But, behold, they will not believe me, nor listen to my voice; for they will say, ‘Yahweh has not appeared to you.’”
verses.2:
Yahweh said to him, “What is that in your hand?”
He said, “A rod.”
verses.3:
He said, “Throw it on the ground.”
He threw it on the ground, and it became a snake; and Moses ran away from it.
verses.4:
Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand, and take it by the tail.”
He stretched out his hand, and took hold of it, and it became a rod in his hand.
verses.5: “That they may believe that Yahweh, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you.”
verses.6:
Yahweh said furthermore to him, “Now put your hand inside your cloak.”
He put his hand inside his cloak, and when he took it out, behold, his hand was leprous, as white as snow.
verses.7:
He said, “Put your hand inside your cloak again.”
He put his hand inside his cloak again, and when he took it out of his cloak, behold, it had turned again as his other flesh.
verses.8: “It will happen, if they will not believe you or listen to the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the latter sign.
verses.9: It will happen, if they will not believe even these two signs or listen to your voice, that you shall take of the water of the river, and pour it on the dry land. The water which you take out of the river will become blood on the dry land.”
verses.10: Moses said to Yahweh, “O Lord, I am not eloquent, neither before now, nor since you have spoken to your servant; for I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.”
verses.11: Yahweh said to him, “Who made man’s mouth? Or who makes one mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Isn’t it I, Yahweh?
verses.12: Now therefore go, and I will be with your mouth, and teach you what you shall speak.”
verses.13: He said, “Oh, Lord, please send someone else.”
verses.14: Yahweh’s anger burned against Moses, and he said, “What about Aaron, your brother, the Levite? I know that he can speak well. Also, behold, he comes out to meet you. When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.
verses.15: You shall speak to him, and put the words in his mouth. I will be with your mouth, and with his mouth, and will teach you what you shall do.
verses.16: He will be your spokesman to the people; and it will happen, that he will be to you a mouth, and you will be to him as God.
verses.17: You shall take this rod in your hand, with which you shall do the signs.”
verses.18:
Moses went and returned to Jethro his father-in-law, and said to him, “Please let me go and return to my brothers who are in Egypt, and see whether they are still alive.”
Jethro said to Moses, “Go in peace.”
verses.19: Yahweh said to Moses in Midian, “Go, return into Egypt; for all the men who sought your life are dead.”
verses.20: Moses took his wife and his sons, and set them on a donkey, and he returned to the land of Egypt. Moses took God’s rod in his hand.
verses.21: Yahweh said to Moses, “When you go back into Egypt, see that you do before Pharaoh all the wonders which I have put in your hand, but I will harden his heart and he will not let the people go.
verses.22: You shall tell Pharaoh, ‘Yahweh says, Israel is my son, my firstborn,
verses.23: and I have said to you, “Let my son go, that he may serve me”; and you have refused to let him go. Behold, I will kill your son, your firstborn.’”
verses.24: On the way at a lodging place, Yahweh met Moses and wanted to kill him.
verses.25: Then Zipporah took a flint, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet; and she said, “Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me.”
verses.26: So he let him alone. Then she said, “You are a bridegroom of blood,” because of the circumcision.
verses.27:
Yahweh said to Aaron, “Go into the wilderness to meet Moses.”
He went, and met him on God’s mountain, and kissed him.
verses.28: Moses told Aaron all Yahweh’s words with which he had sent him, and all the signs with which he had instructed him.
verses.29: Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel.
verses.30: Aaron spoke all the words which Yahweh had spoken to Moses, and did the signs in the sight of the people.
verses.31: The people believed, and when they heard that Yahweh had visited the children of Israel, and that he had seen their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshiped.

verses.1: Afterward Moses and Aaron came, and said to Pharaoh, “This is what Yahweh, the God of Israel, says, ‘Let my people go, that they may hold a feast to me in the wilderness.’”
verses.2: Pharaoh said, “Who is Yahweh, that I should listen to his voice to let Israel go? I don’t know Yahweh, and moreover I will not let Israel go.”
verses.3: They said, “The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please let us go three days’ journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to Yahweh, our God, lest he fall on us with pestilence, or with the sword.”
verses.4: The king of Egypt said to them, “Why do you, Moses and Aaron, take the people from their work? Get back to your burdens!”
verses.5: Pharaoh said, “Behold, the people of the land are now many, and you make them rest from their burdens.”
verses.6: The same day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people, and their officers, saying,
verses.7: “You shall no longer give the people straw to make brick, as before. Let them go and gather straw for themselves.
verses.8: The number of the bricks, which they made before, you require from them. You shall not diminish anything of it, for they are idle; therefore they cry, saying, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to our God.’
verses.9: Let heavier work be laid on the men, that they may labor in it; and don’t let them pay any attention to lying words.”
verses.10: The taskmasters of the people went out, and their officers, and they spoke to the people, saying, “This is what Pharaoh says: ‘I will not give you straw.
verses.11: Go yourselves, get straw where you can find it, for nothing of your work shall be diminished.’”
verses.12: So the people were scattered abroad throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
verses.13: The taskmasters were urgent saying, “Fulfill your work quota daily, as when there was straw!”
verses.14: The officers of the children of Israel, whom Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, and demanded, “Why haven’t you fulfilled your quota both yesterday and today, in making brick as before?”
verses.15: Then the officers of the children of Israel came and cried to Pharaoh, saying, “Why do you deal this way with your servants?
verses.16: No straw is given to your servants, and they tell us, ‘Make brick!’ and behold, your servants are beaten; but the fault is in your own people.”
verses.17: But he said, “You are idle! You are idle! Therefore you say, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to Yahweh.’
verses.18: Go therefore now, and work, for no straw shall be given to you, yet you shall deliver the same number of bricks!”
verses.19: The officers of the children of Israel saw that they were in trouble, when it was said, “You shall not diminish anything from your daily quota of bricks!”
verses.20: They met Moses and Aaron, who stood in the way, as they came out from Pharaoh:
verses.21: and they said to them, “May Yahweh look at you, and judge, because you have made us a stench to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to kill us.”
verses.22: Moses returned to Yahweh, and said, “Lord, why have you brought trouble on this people? Why is it that you have sent me?
verses.23: For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has brought trouble on this people; and you have not rescued your people at all.”

verses.1: Yahweh said to Moses, “Now you shall see what I will do to Pharaoh, for by a strong hand he shall let them go, and by a strong hand he shall drive them out of his land.”
verses.2: God spoke to Moses, and said to him, “I am Yahweh;
verses.3: and I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, as God Almighty; but by my name Yahweh I was not known to them.
verses.4: I have also established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their travels, in which they lived as aliens.
verses.5: Moreover I have heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians keep in bondage, and I have remembered my covenant.
verses.6: Therefore tell the children of Israel, ‘I am Yahweh, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments:
verses.7: and I will take you to me for a people, and I will be to you a God; and you shall know that I am Yahweh your God, who brings you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.
verses.8: I will bring you into the land which I swore to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it to you for a heritage: I am Yahweh.’”
verses.9: Moses spoke so to the children of Israel, but they didn’t listen to Moses for anguish of spirit, and for cruel bondage.
verses.10: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.11: “Go in, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.”
verses.12: Moses spoke before Yahweh, saying, “Behold, the children of Israel haven’t listened to me. How then shall Pharaoh listen to me, who am of uncircumcised lips?”
verses.13: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, and gave them a command to the children of Israel, and to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
verses.14: These are the heads of their fathers’ houses. The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, and Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi; these are the families of Reuben.
verses.15: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman; these are the families of Simeon.
verses.16: These are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari; and the years of the life of Levi were one hundred thirty-seven years.
verses.17: The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, according to their families.
verses.18: The sons of Kohath: Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel; and the years of the life of Kohath were one hundred thirty-three years.
verses.19: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to their generations.
verses.20: Amram took Jochebed his father’s sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram were a hundred and thirty-seven years.
verses.21: The sons of Izhar: Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.
verses.22: The sons of Uzziel: Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Sithri.
verses.23: Aaron took Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, as his wife; and she bore him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
verses.24: The sons of Korah: Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph; these are the families of the Korahites.
verses.25: Eleazar Aaron’s son took one of the daughters of Putiel as his wife; and she bore him Phinehas. These are the heads of the fathers’ houses of the Levites according to their families.
verses.26: These are that Aaron and Moses, to whom Yahweh said, “Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt according to their armies.”
verses.27: These are those who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the children of Israel from Egypt. These are that Moses and Aaron.
verses.28: On the day when Yahweh spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
verses.29: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying, “I am Yahweh. Speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I speak to you.”
verses.30: Moses said before Yahweh, “Behold, I am of uncircumcised lips, and how shall Pharaoh listen to me?”

verses.1: Yahweh said to Moses, “Behold, I have made you as God to Pharaoh; and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet.
verses.2: You shall speak all that I command you; and Aaron your brother shall speak to Pharaoh, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.
verses.3: I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.
verses.4: But Pharaoh will not listen to you, and I will lay my hand on Egypt, and bring out my armies, my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.
verses.5: The Egyptians shall know that I am Yahweh, when I stretch out my hand on Egypt, and bring out the children of Israel from among them.”
verses.6: Moses and Aaron did so. As Yahweh commanded them, so they did.
verses.7: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.
verses.8: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
verses.9: “When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, ‘Perform a miracle!’ then you shall tell Aaron, ‘Take your rod, and cast it down before Pharaoh, that it become a serpent.’”
verses.10: Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and they did so, as Yahweh had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.
verses.11: Then Pharaoh also called for the wise men and the sorcerers. They also, the magicians of Egypt, did the same thing with their enchantments.
verses.12: For they each cast down their rods, and they became serpents: but Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods.
verses.13: Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he didn’t listen to them; as Yahweh had spoken.
verses.14: Yahweh said to Moses, “Pharaoh’s heart is stubborn. He refuses to let the people go.
verses.15: Go to Pharaoh in the morning. Behold, he goes out to the water; and you shall stand by the river’s bank to meet him; and the rod which was turned to a serpent you shall take in your hand.
verses.16: You shall tell him, ‘Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying, “Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness:” and behold, until now you haven’t listened.
verses.17: Yahweh says, “In this you shall know that I am Yahweh. Behold, I will strike with the rod that is in my hand on the waters which are in the river, and they shall be turned to blood.
verses.18: The fish that are in the river shall die, and the river shall become foul; and the Egyptians shall loathe to drink water from the river.”’”
verses.19: Yahweh said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Take your rod, and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their streams, and over their pools, and over all their ponds of water, that they may become blood; and there shall be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood and in vessels of stone.’”
verses.20: Moses and Aaron did so, as Yahweh commanded; and he lifted up the rod, and struck the waters that were in the river, in the sight of Pharaoh, and in the sight of his servants; and all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood.
verses.21: The fish that were in the river died; and the river became foul, and the Egyptians couldn’t drink water from the river; and the blood was throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.22: The magicians of Egypt did the same thing with their enchantments; and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he didn’t listen to them; as Yahweh had spoken.
verses.23: Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he didn’t even take this to heart.
verses.24: All the Egyptians dug around the river for water to drink; for they couldn’t drink the river water.
verses.25: Seven days were fulfilled, after Yahweh had struck the river.

verses.1: Yahweh spoke to Moses, Go in to Pharaoh, and tell him, “This is what Yahweh says, ‘Let my people go, that they may serve me.
verses.2: If you refuse to let them go, behold, I will plague all your borders with frogs:
verses.3: and the river shall swarm with frogs, which shall go up and come into your house, and into your bedroom, and on your bed, and into the house of your servants, and on your people, and into your ovens, and into your kneading troughs:
verses.4: and the frogs shall come up both on you, and on your people, and on all your servants.’”
verses.5: Yahweh said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your hand with your rod over the rivers, over the streams, and over the pools, and cause frogs to come up on the land of Egypt.’”
verses.6: Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt; and the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt.
verses.7: The magicians did the same thing with their enchantments, and brought up frogs on the land of Egypt.
verses.8: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said, “Entreat Yahweh, that he take away the frogs from me, and from my people; and I will let the people go, that they may sacrifice to Yahweh.”
verses.9: Moses said to Pharaoh, “I give you the honor of setting the time that I should pray for you, and for your servants, and for your people, that the frogs be destroyed from you and your houses, and remain in the river only.”
verses.10:
He said, “Tomorrow.”
He said, “Be it according to your word, that you may know that there is no one like Yahweh our God.
verses.11: The frogs shall depart from you, and from your houses, and from your servants, and from your people. They shall remain in the river only.”
verses.12: Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried to Yahweh concerning the frogs which he had brought on Pharaoh.
verses.13: Yahweh did according to the word of Moses, and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courts, and out of the fields.
verses.14: They gathered them together in heaps, and the land stank.
verses.15: But when Pharaoh saw that there was a respite, he hardened his heart, and didn’t listen to them, as Yahweh had spoken.
verses.16: Yahweh said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your rod, and strike the dust of the earth, that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.’”
verses.17: They did so; and Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod, and struck the dust of the earth, and there were lice on man, and on animal; all the dust of the earth became lice throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.18: The magicians tried with their enchantments to produce lice, but they couldn’t. There were lice on man, and on animal.
verses.19: Then the magicians said to Pharaoh, “This is God’s finger:” and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he didn’t listen to them; as Yahweh had spoken.
verses.20: Yahweh said to Moses, “Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh; behold, he comes out to the water; and tell him, ‘This is what Yahweh says, “Let my people go, that they may serve me.
verses.21: Else, if you will not let my people go, behold, I will send swarms of flies on you, and on your servants, and on your people, and into your houses: and the houses of the Egyptians shall be full of swarms of flies, and also the ground whereon they are.
verses.22: I will set apart in that day the land of Goshen, in which my people dwell, that no swarms of flies shall be there; to the end you may know that I am Yahweh on the earth.
verses.23: I will put a division between my people and your people: by tomorrow shall this sign be.”’”
verses.24: Yahweh did so; and there came grievous swarms of flies into the house of Pharaoh, and into his servants’ houses: and in all the land of Egypt the land was corrupted by reason of the swarms of flies.
verses.25: Pharaoh called for Moses and for Aaron, and said, “Go, sacrifice to your God in the land!”
verses.26: Moses said, “It isn’t appropriate to do so; for we shall sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians to Yahweh our God. Behold, shall we sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and won’t they stone us?
verses.27: We will go three days’ journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to Yahweh our God, as he shall command us.”
verses.28: Pharaoh said, “I will let you go, that you may sacrifice to Yahweh your God in the wilderness, only you shall not go very far away. Pray for me.”
verses.29: Moses said, “Behold, I go out from you, and I will pray to Yahweh that the swarms of flies may depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people, tomorrow; only don’t let Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more in not letting the people go to sacrifice to Yahweh.”
verses.30: Moses went out from Pharaoh, and prayed to Yahweh.
verses.31: Yahweh did according to the word of Moses, and he removed the swarms of flies from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people. There remained not one.
verses.32: Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also, and he didn’t let the people go.

verses.1: Then Yahweh said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, and tell him, ‘This is what Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, says: “Let my people go, that they may serve me.
verses.2: For if you refuse to let them go, and hold them still,
verses.3: behold, Yahweh’s hand is on your livestock which are in the field, on the horses, on the donkeys, on the camels, on the herds, and on the flocks with a very grievous pestilence.
verses.4: Yahweh will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt; and nothing shall die of all that belongs to the children of Israel.”’”
verses.5: Yahweh appointed a set time, saying, “Tomorrow Yahweh shall do this thing in the land.”
verses.6: Yahweh did that thing on the next day; and all the livestock of Egypt died, but of the livestock of the children of Israel, not one died.
verses.7: Pharaoh sent, and, behold, there was not so much as one of the livestock of the Israelites dead. But the heart of Pharaoh was stubborn, and he didn’t let the people go.
verses.8: Yahweh said to Moses and to Aaron, “Take to you handfuls of ashes of the furnace, and let Moses sprinkle it toward the sky in the sight of Pharaoh.
verses.9: It shall become small dust over all the land of Egypt, and shall be a boil breaking out with boils on man and on animal, throughout all the land of Egypt.”
verses.10: They took ashes of the furnace, and stood before Pharaoh; and Moses sprinkled it up toward the sky; and it became a boil breaking out with boils on man and on animal.
verses.11: The magicians couldn’t stand before Moses because of the boils; for the boils were on the magicians, and on all the Egyptians.
verses.12: Yahweh hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he didn’t listen to them, as Yahweh had spoken to Moses.
verses.13: Yahweh said to Moses, “Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh, and tell him, ‘This is what Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, says: “Let my people go, that they may serve me.
verses.14: For this time I will send all my plagues against your heart, against your officials, and against your people; that you may know that there is no one like me in all the earth.
verses.15: For now I would have stretched out my hand, and struck you and your people with pestilence, and you would have been cut off from the earth;
verses.16: but indeed for this cause I have made you stand: to show you my power, and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth;
verses.17: as you still exalt yourself against my people, that you won’t let them go.
verses.18: Behold, tomorrow about this time I will cause it to rain a very grievous hail, such as has not been in Egypt since the day it was founded even until now.
verses.19: Now therefore command that all of your livestock and all that you have in the field be brought into shelter. Every man and animal that is found in the field, and isn’t brought home, the hail shall come down on them, and they shall die.”’”
verses.20: Those who feared Yahweh’s word among the servants of Pharaoh made their servants and their livestock flee into the houses.
verses.21: Whoever didn’t respect Yahweh’s word left his servants and his livestock in the field.
verses.22: Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky, that there may be hail in all the land of Egypt, on man, and on animal, and on every herb of the field, throughout the land of Egypt.”
verses.23: Moses stretched out his rod toward the heavens, and Yahweh sent thunder, hail, and lightning flashed down to the earth. Yahweh rained hail on the land of Egypt.
verses.24: So there was very severe hail, and lightning mixed with the hail, such as had not been in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.
verses.25: The hail struck throughout all the land of Egypt all that was in the field, both man and animal; and the hail struck every herb of the field, and broke every tree of the field.
verses.26: Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, there was no hail.
verses.27: Pharaoh sent, and called for Moses and Aaron, and said to them, “I have sinned this time. Yahweh is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.
verses.28: Pray to Yahweh; for there has been enough of mighty thunderings and hail. I will let you go, and you shall stay no longer.”
verses.29: Moses said to him, “As soon as I have gone out of the city, I will spread abroad my hands to Yahweh. The thunders shall cease, and there will not be any more hail; that you may know that the earth is Yahweh’s.
verses.30: But as for you and your servants, I know that you don’t yet fear Yahweh God.”
verses.31: The flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was in the ear, and the flax was in bloom.
verses.32: But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they had not grown up.
verses.33: Moses went out of the city from Pharaoh, and spread abroad his hands to Yahweh; and the thunders and hail ceased, and the rain was not poured on the earth.
verses.34: When Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunders had ceased, he sinned yet more, and hardened his heart, he and his servants.
verses.35: The heart of Pharaoh was hardened, and he didn’t let the children of Israel go, just as Yahweh had spoken through Moses.

verses.1: Yahweh said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants, that I may show these my signs among them,
verses.2: and that you may tell in the hearing of your son, and of your son’s son, what things I have done to Egypt, and my signs which I have done among them; that you may know that I am Yahweh.”
verses.3: Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and said to him, “This is what Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go, that they may serve me.
verses.4: Or else, if you refuse to let my people go, behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your country,
verses.5: and they shall cover the surface of the earth, so that one won’t be able to see the earth. They shall eat the residue of that which has escaped, which remains to you from the hail, and shall eat every tree which grows for you out of the field.
