that he has purposed against the land of the Chaldeans:
Surely they will drag them away,
even the little ones of the flock.
Surely he will make their habitation desolate over them.
verses.46:
At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth trembles;
and the cry is heard among the nations.

verses.1:
Yahweh says:
“Behold, I will raise up against Babylon,
and against those who dwell in Lebkamai, a destroying wind.
verses.3:
Against him who bends, let the archer bend his bow,
also against him who lifts himself up in his coat of mail.
Don’t spare her young men!
Utterly destroy all her army!
verses.4:
They will fall down slain in the land of the Chaldeans,
and thrust through in her streets.
verses.6:
“Flee out of the middle of Babylon!
Everyone save his own life!
Don’t be cut off in her iniquity;
for it is the time of Yahweh’s vengeance.
He will render to her a recompense.
verses.7:
Babylon has been a golden cup in Yahweh’s hand,
who made all the earth drunk.
The nations have drunk of her wine;
therefore the nations have gone mad.
verses.8:
Babylon has suddenly fallen and been destroyed!
Wail for her!
Take balm for her pain.
Perhaps she may be healed.
verses.10:
‘Yahweh has produced our righteousness:
come, and let us declare in Zion the work of Yahweh our God.’
verses.12:
Set up a standard against the walls of Babylon!
Make the watch strong!
Set the watchmen,
and prepare the ambushes;
for Yahweh has both purposed and done
that which he spoke concerning the inhabitants of Babylon.
verses.13:
You who dwell on many waters, abundant in treasures,
your end has come, the measure of your covetousness.
verses.14:
Yahweh of Armies has sworn by himself, saying,
‘Surely I will fill you with men,
as with the canker worm;
and they will lift up a shout against you.’
verses.15:
“He has made the earth by his power.
He has established the world by his wisdom.
By his understanding he has stretched out the heavens.
verses.16:
When he utters his voice,
there is a roar of waters in the heavens,
and he causes the vapors to ascend from the ends of the earth.
He makes lightning for the rain,
and brings the wind out of his treasuries.
verses.18:
They are vanity,
a work of delusion.
In the time of their visitation, they will perish.
verses.19:
The portion of Jacob is not like these,
for he is the former of all things;
including the tribe of his inheritance:
Yahweh of Armies is his name.
verses.20:
“You are my battle ax and weapons of war.
With you I will break the nations into pieces.
With you I will destroy kingdoms.
verses.21:
With you I will break in pieces
the horse and his rider.
verses.22:
With you I will break in pieces
the chariot and him who rides therein.
With you I will break in pieces
man and woman.
With you I will break in pieces
the old man and the youth.
With you I will break in pieces
the young man and the virgin.
verses.23:
With you I will break in pieces
the shepherd and his flock.
With you I will break in pieces
the farmer and his yoke.
With you will I break in pieces
governors and deputies.
verses.24: “I will render to Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight,” says Yahweh.
verses.25:
“Behold, I am against you, destroying mountain,” says Yahweh,
“which destroys all the earth.
I will stretch out my hand on you,
roll you down from the rocks,
and will make you a burned mountain.
verses.27:
“Set up a standard in the land!
Blow the trumpet among the nations!
Prepare the nations against her!
Call together against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz!
Appoint a marshal against her!
Cause the horses to come up as the rough canker worm!
verses.28:
Prepare against her the nations,
the kings of the Medes, its governors, and all its deputies, and all the land of their dominion!
verses.30:
The mighty men of Babylon have stopped fighting,
they remain in their strongholds.
Their might has failed.
They have become as women.
Her dwelling places are set on fire.
Her bars are broken.
verses.31:
One runner will run to meet another,
and one messenger to meet another,
to show the king of Babylon that his city is taken on every quarter.
verses.32:
So the passages are seized.
They have burned the reeds with fire.
The men of war are frightened.”
verses.33:
For Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says:
“The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time when it is trodden.
Yet a little while, and the time of harvest comes for her.”
verses.34:
“Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon has devoured me.
He has crushed me.
He has made me an empty vessel.
He has, like a monster, swallowed me up.
He has filled his mouth with my delicacies.
He has cast me out.
verses.35:
May the violence done to me and to my flesh be on Babylon!”
the inhabitant of Zion will say; and,
“May my blood be on the inhabitants of Chaldea!”
will Jerusalem say.
verses.36:
Therefore Yahweh says:
“Behold, I will plead your cause,
and take vengeance for you.
I will dry up her sea,
and make her fountain dry.
verses.37:
Babylon will become heaps,
a dwelling place for jackals,
an astonishment, and a hissing,
without inhabitant.
verses.38:
They will roar together like young lions.
They will growl as lions’ cubs.
verses.39:
When they are heated, I will make their feast,
and I will make them drunk,
that they may rejoice,
and sleep a perpetual sleep,
and not wake up,” says Yahweh.
verses.40:
“I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter,
like rams with male goats.
verses.41:
“How Sheshach is taken!
How the praise of the whole earth seized!
How Babylon has become a desolation among the nations!
verses.42:
The sea has come up on Babylon.
She is covered with the multitude of its waves.
verses.43:
Her cities have become a desolation,
a dry land, and a desert,
a land in which no man dwells.
No son of man passes by it.
verses.44:
I will execute judgment on Bel in Babylon,
and I will bring out of his mouth that which he has swallowed up.
The nations will not flow any more to him.
Yes, the wall of Babylon will fall.
verses.45:
“My people, go away from the middle of her,
and each of you save yourselves from Yahweh’s fierce anger.
verses.46:
Don’t let your heart faint.
Don’t fear for the news that will be heard in the land.
For news will come one year,
and after that in another year news will come,
and violence in the land,
ruler against ruler.
verses.48:
Then the heavens and the earth,
and all that is therein,
will sing for joy over Babylon;
for the destroyers will come to her from the north,” says Yahweh.
verses.49:
“As Babylon has caused the slain of Israel to fall,
so the slain of all the land will fall at Babylon.
verses.50:
You who have escaped the sword, go!
Don’t stand still!
Remember Yahweh from afar,
and let Jerusalem come into your mind.”
verses.51:
“We are confounded,
because we have heard reproach.
Confusion has covered our faces,
for strangers have come into the sanctuaries of Yahweh’s house.”
verses.53:
Though Babylon should mount up to the sky,
and though she should fortify the height of her strength,
yet destroyers will come to her from me,” says Yahweh.
verses.54:
“The sound of a cry comes from Babylon,
and of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans!
verses.55:
For Yahweh lays Babylon waste,
and destroys out of her the great voice!
Their waves roar like many waters.
The noise of their voice is uttered.
verses.56:
For the destroyer has come on her,
even on Babylon.
Her mighty men are taken.
Their bows are broken in pieces,
for Yahweh is a God of retribution.
He will surely repay.
verses.57:
I will make her princes, her wise men,
her governors, her deputies, and her mighty men drunk.
They will sleep a perpetual sleep,
and not wake up,”
says the King, whose name is Yahweh of Armies.
verses.58:
Yahweh of Armies says:
“The wide walls of Babylon will be utterly overthrown.
Her high gates will be burned with fire.
The peoples will labor for vanity,
and the nations for the fire;
and they will be weary.”
verses.59: The word which Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah the king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Now Seraiah was chief quartermaster.
verses.60: Jeremiah wrote in a book all the evil that should come on Babylon, even all these words that are written concerning Babylon.
verses.61: Jeremiah said to Seraiah, “When you come to Babylon, then see that you read all these words,
verses.62: and say, ‘Yahweh, you have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, that no one will dwell in it, neither man nor animal, but that it will be desolate forever.’
verses.63: It will be, when you have finished reading this book, that you shall bind a stone to it, and cast it into the middle of the Euphrates.
verses.64:
Then you shall say, ‘Thus will Babylon sink, and will not rise again because of the evil that I will bring on her; and they will be weary.’”
Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.

verses.1: Listen to this word which I take up for a lamentation over you, O house of Israel.
verses.3:
For thus says the Lord Yahweh:
“The city that went out a thousand shall have a hundred left,
and that which went out one hundred shall have ten left to the house of Israel.”
verses.4:
For Yahweh says to the house of Israel:
“Seek me, and you will live;
verses.5:
but don’t seek Bethel,
nor enter into Gilgal,
and don’t pass to Beersheba:
for Gilgal shall surely go into captivity,
and Bethel shall come to nothing.
verses.7:
You who turn justice to wormwood,
and cast down righteousness to the earth:
verses.8:
seek him who made the Pleiades and Orion,
and turns the shadow of death into the morning,
and makes the day dark with night;
who calls for the waters of the sea,
and pours them out on the surface of the earth, Yahweh is his name,
verses.9:
who brings sudden destruction on the strong,
so that destruction comes on the fortress.
verses.10:
They hate him who reproves in the gate,
and they abhor him who speaks blamelessly.
verses.11:
Therefore, because you trample on the poor,
and take taxes from him of wheat:
You have built houses of cut stone,
but you will not dwell in them.
You have planted pleasant vineyards,
but you shall not drink their wine.
verses.12:
For I know how many your offenses,
and how great are your sins—
you who afflict the just,
who take a bribe,
and who turn away the needy in the courts.
verses.13:
Therefore a prudent person keeps silent in such a time,
for it is an evil time.
verses.14:
Seek good, and not evil,
that you may live;
and so Yahweh, the God of Armies, will be with you,
as you say.
verses.15:
Hate evil, love good,
and establish justice in the courts.
It may be that Yahweh, the God of Armies, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.”
verses.16:
Therefore Yahweh, the God of Armies, the Lord, says:
“Wailing will be in all the wide ways;
and they will say in all the streets, ‘Alas! Alas!’
and they will call the farmer to mourning,
and those who are skillful in lamentation to wailing.
verses.17:
In all vineyards there will be wailing;
for I will pass through the middle of you,” says Yahweh.
verses.18:
“Woe to you who desire the day of Yahweh!
Why do you long for the day of Yahweh?
It is darkness,
and not light.
verses.19:
As if a man fled from a lion,
and a bear met him;
Or he went into the house and leaned his hand on the wall,
and a snake bit him.
verses.20:
Won’t the day of Yahweh be darkness, and not light?
Even very dark, and no brightness in it?
verses.21:
I hate, I despise your feasts,
and I can’t stand your solemn assemblies.
verses.23:
Take away from me the noise of your songs!
I will not listen to the music of your harps.
verses.24:
But let justice roll on like rivers,
and righteousness like a mighty stream.
verses.25: “Did you bring to me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness forty years, house of Israel?
verses.26: You also carried the tent of your king and the shrine of your images, the star of your god, which you made for yourselves.
verses.27: Therefore will I cause you to go into captivity beyond Damascus,” says Yahweh, whose name is the God of Armies.

verses.1:
Woe to those who are at ease in Zion,
and to those who are secure on the mountain of Samaria,
the notable men of the chief of the nations,
to whom the house of Israel come!
verses.3:
Those who put far away the evil day,
and cause the seat of violence to come near;
verses.4:
Who lie on beds of ivory,
and stretch themselves on their couches,
and eat the lambs out of the flock,
and the calves out of the middle of the stall;
verses.5:
who strum on the strings of a harp;
who invent for themselves instruments of music, like David;
verses.7:
Therefore they will now go captive with the first who go captive;
and the feasting and lounging will end.
verses.8:
“The Lord Yahweh has sworn by himself,” says Yahweh, the God of Armies:
“I abhor the pride of Jacob,
and detest his fortresses.
Therefore I will deliver up the city with all that is in it.
verses.9:
It will happen, if there remain ten men in one house,
that they shall die.
verses.10: “When a man’s relative carries him, even he who burns him, to bring bodies out of the house, and asks him who is in the innermost parts of the house, ‘Is there yet any with you?’ And he says, ‘No;’ then he will say, ‘Hush! Indeed we must not mention Yahweh’s name.’
verses.11:
“For, behold, Yahweh commands, and the great house will be smashed to pieces,
and the little house into bits.
verses.12:
Do horses run on the rocky crags?
Does one plow there with oxen?
But you have turned justice into poison,
and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness;
verses.13:
you who rejoice in a thing of nothing, who say,
‘Haven’t we taken for ourselves horns by our own strength?’

verses.1: Thus the Lord Yahweh showed me: and behold, he formed locusts in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth; and behold, it was the latter growth after the king’s harvest.
verses.2: When they finished eating the grass of the land, then I said, “Lord Yahweh, forgive, I beg you! How could Jacob stand? For he is small.”
verses.3: Yahweh relented concerning this. “It shall not be,” says Yahweh.
verses.4: Thus the Lord Yahweh showed me and behold, the Lord Yahweh called for judgment by fire; and it dried up the great deep, and would have devoured the land.
verses.5: Then I said, “Lord Yahweh, stop, I beg you! How could Jacob stand? For he is small.”
verses.6: Yahweh relented concerning this. “This also shall not be,” says the Lord Yahweh.
verses.7: Thus he showed me and behold, the Lord stood beside a wall made by a plumb line, with a plumb line in his hand.
verses.8:
Yahweh said to me, “Amos, what do you see?”
I said, “A plumb line.”
Then the Lord said, “Behold, I will set a plumb line in the middle of my people Israel. I will not again pass by them any more.
verses.9: The high places of Isaac will be desolate, the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.”
verses.10: Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, “Amos has conspired against you in the middle of the house of Israel. The land is not able to bear all his words.
verses.11: For Amos says, ‘Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land.’”
verses.12: Amaziah also said to Amos, “You seer, go, flee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there:
verses.13: but don’t prophesy again any more at Bethel; for it is the king’s sanctuary, and it is a royal house!”
verses.14: Then Amos answered Amaziah, “I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son; but I was a herdsman, and a farmer of sycamore figs;
verses.15: and Yahweh took me from following the flock, and Yahweh said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to my people Israel.’
verses.16: Now therefore listen to Yahweh’s word: ‘You say, Don’t prophesy against Israel, and don’t preach against the house of Isaac.’
verses.17: Therefore Yahweh says: ‘Your wife shall be a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword, and your land shall be divided by line; and you yourself shall die in a land that is unclean, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land.’”

verses.1: Thus the Lord Yahweh showed me: behold, a basket of summer fruit.
verses.2:
He said, “Amos, what do you see?”
I said, “A basket of summer fruit.”
Then Yahweh said to me,
“The end has come on my people Israel.
I will not again pass by them any more.
verses.3:
The songs of the temple will be wailings in that day,” says the Lord Yahweh.
“The dead bodies will be many. In every place they will throw them out with silence.
verses.4:
Hear this, you who desire to swallow up the needy,
and cause the poor of the land to fail,
verses.5:
Saying, ‘When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell grain?
And the Sabbath, that we may market wheat,
making the ephah small, and the shekel large,
and dealing falsely with balances of deceit;
verses.6:
that we may buy the poor for silver,
and the needy for a pair of shoes,
and sell the sweepings with the wheat?’”
verses.7:
Yahweh has sworn by the pride of Jacob,
“Surely I will never forget any of their works.
verses.8:
Won’t the land tremble for this,
and everyone mourn who dwells in it?
Yes, it will rise up wholly like the River;
and it will be stirred up and sink again, like the River of Egypt.
verses.9:
It will happen in that day,” says the Lord Yahweh,
“that I will cause the sun to go down at noon,
and I will darken the earth in the clear day.
verses.10:
I will turn your feasts into mourning,
and all your songs into lamentation;
and I will make you wear sackcloth on all your bodies,
and baldness on every head.
I will make it like the mourning for an only son,
and its end like a bitter day.
verses.11:
Behold, the days come,” says the Lord Yahweh,
“that I will send a famine in the land,
not a famine of bread,
nor a thirst for water,
but of hearing Yahweh’s words.
verses.12:
They will wander from sea to sea,
and from the north even to the east;
they will run back and forth to seek Yahweh’s word,
and will not find it.
verses.13:
In that day the beautiful virgins
and the young men will faint for thirst.
verses.14:
Those who swear by the sin of Samaria,
and say, ‘As your god, Dan, lives;’
and, ‘As the way of Beersheba lives;’
they will fall, and never rise up again.”

verses.1: I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and he said, “Strike the tops of the pillars, that the thresholds may shake; and break them in pieces on the head of all of them; and I will kill the last of them with the sword: there shall not one of them flee away, and there shall not one of them escape.
verses.2: Though they dig into Sheol, there my hand will take them; and though they climb up to heaven, there I will bring them down.
verses.3: Though they hide themselves in the top of Carmel, I will search and take them out there; and though they be hidden from my sight in the bottom of the sea, there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.
verses.4: Though they go into captivity before their enemies, there I will command the sword, and it will kill them. I will set my eyes on them for evil, and not for good.
verses.5: For the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, is he who touches the land and it melts, and all who dwell in it will mourn; and it will rise up wholly like the River, and will sink again, like the River of Egypt.
verses.6: It is he who builds his rooms in the heavens, and has founded his vault on the earth; he who calls for the waters of the sea, and pours them out on the surface of the earth; Yahweh is his name.
verses.7: Are you not like the children of the Ethiopians to me, children of Israel?” says Yahweh. “Haven’t I brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir?
verses.8: Behold, the eyes of the Lord Yahweh are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the surface of the earth; except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,” says Yahweh.
verses.9: “For, behold, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all the nations, as grain is sifted in a sieve, yet not the least kernel will fall on the earth.
verses.10: All the sinners of my people will die by the sword, who say, ‘Evil won’t overtake nor meet us.’
verses.11: In that day I will raise up the tent of David who is fallen, and close up its breaches, and I will raise up its ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old;
verses.12: that they may possess the remnant of Edom, and all the nations who are called by my name,” says Yahweh who does this.
verses.13:
“Behold, the days come,” says Yahweh,
“that the plowman shall overtake the reaper,
and the one treading grapes him who sows seed;
and sweet wine will drip from the mountains,
and flow from the hills.
verses.14:
I will bring my people Israel back from captivity,
and they will rebuild the ruined cities, and inhabit them;
and they will plant vineyards, and drink wine from them.
They shall also make gardens,
and eat their fruit.
verses.15:
I will plant them on their land,
and they will no more be plucked up out of their land which I have given them,”
says Yahweh your God.

verses.1: The vision of Obadiah. This is what the Lord Yahweh says about Edom. We have heard news from Yahweh, and an ambassador is sent among the nations, saying, “Arise, and let’s rise up against her in battle.
Now Yahweh’s word came to Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,
verses.2: “Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and preach against it, for their wickedness has come up before me.”
verses.3: But Jonah rose up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of Yahweh. He went down to Joppa, and found a ship going to Tarshish; so he paid its fare, and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish from the presence of Yahweh.
verses.4: But Yahweh sent out a great wind on the sea, and there was a mighty storm on the sea, so that the ship was likely to break up.
verses.5: Then the mariners were afraid, and every man cried to his god. They threw the cargo that was in the ship into the sea to lighten the ship. But Jonah had gone down into the innermost parts of the ship, and he was laying down, and was fast asleep.
verses.6: So the ship master came to him, and said to him, “What do you mean, sleeper? Arise, call on your God! Maybe your God will notice us, so that we won’t perish.”
verses.7: They all said to each other, “Come, let us cast lots, that we may know who is responsible for this evil that is on us.” So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
verses.8: Then they asked him, “Tell us, please, for whose cause this evil is on us. What is your occupation? Where do you come from? What is your country? Of what people are you?”
verses.9: He said to them, “I am a Hebrew, and I fear Yahweh, the God of heaven, who has made the sea and the dry land.”
verses.10: Then the men were exceedingly afraid, and said to him, “What have you done?” For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of Yahweh, because he had told them.
verses.11: Then they said to him, “What shall we do to you, that the sea may be calm to us?” For the sea grew more and more stormy.
verses.12: He said to them, “Take me up, and throw me into the sea. Then the sea will be calm for you; for I know that because of me this great storm is on you.”
verses.13: Nevertheless the men rowed hard to get them back to the land; but they could not, for the sea grew more and more stormy against them.
verses.14: Therefore they cried to Yahweh, and said, “We beg you, Yahweh, we beg you, don’t let us die for this man’s life, and don’t lay on us innocent blood; for you, Yahweh, have done as it pleased you.”
verses.15: So they took up Jonah, and threw him into the sea; and the sea ceased its raging.
verses.16: Then the men feared Yahweh exceedingly; and they offered a sacrifice to Yahweh, and made vows.
verses.17: Yahweh prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

verses.1: Then Jonah prayed to Yahweh, his God, out of the fish’s belly.
verses.2:
He said,
“I called because of my affliction to Yahweh.
He answered me.
Out of the belly of Sheol I cried.
You heard my voice.
verses.3:
For you threw me into the depths,
in the heart of the seas.
The flood was all around me.
All your waves and your billows passed over me.
verses.4:
I said, ‘I have been banished from your sight;
yet I will look again toward your holy temple.’
verses.5:
The waters surrounded me,
even to the soul.
The deep was around me.
The weeds were wrapped around my head.
verses.6:
I went down to the bottoms of the mountains.
The earth barred me in forever:
yet have you brought up my life from the pit, Yahweh my God.
verses.7:
“When my soul fainted within me, I remembered Yahweh.
My prayer came in to you, into your holy temple.
verses.8: Those who regard lying vanities forsake their own mercy.
verses.9:
But I will sacrifice to you with the voice of thanksgiving.
I will pay that which I have vowed.
Salvation belongs to Yahweh.”
verses.10: Then Yahweh spoke to the fish, and it vomited out Jonah on the dry land.

verses.1: Yahweh’s word came to Jonah the second time, saying,
verses.2: “Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and preach to it the message that I give you.”
verses.3: So Jonah arose, and went to Nineveh, according to Yahweh’s word. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, three days’ journey across.
verses.4: Jonah began to enter into the city a day’s journey, and he cried out, and said, “In forty days, Nineveh will be overthrown!”
verses.5: The people of Nineveh believed God; and they proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from their greatest even to their least.
verses.6: The news reached the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and took off his royal robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
verses.7: He made a proclamation and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, “Let neither man nor animal, herd nor flock, taste anything; let them not feed, nor drink water;
verses.8: but let them be covered with sackcloth, both man and animal, and let them cry mightily to God. Yes, let them turn everyone from his evil way, and from the violence that is in his hands.
verses.9: Who knows whether God will not turn and relent, and turn away from his fierce anger, so that we might not perish?”
verses.10: God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way. God relented of the disaster which he said he would do to them, and he didn’t do it.

verses.1: But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was angry.
verses.2: He prayed to Yahweh, and said, “Please, Yahweh, wasn’t this what I said when I was still in my own country? Therefore I hurried to flee to Tarshish, for I knew that you are a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and you relent of doing harm.
verses.3: Therefore now, Yahweh, take, I beg you, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live.”
verses.4: Yahweh said, “Is it right for you to be angry?”
verses.5: Then Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and there made himself a booth, and sat under it in the shade, until he might see what would become of the city.
verses.6: Yahweh God prepared a vine, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shade over his head, to deliver him from his discomfort. So Jonah was exceedingly glad because of the vine.
verses.7: But God prepared a worm at dawn the next day, and it chewed on the vine, so that it withered.
verses.8: When the sun arose, God prepared a sultry east wind; and the sun beat on Jonah’s head, so that he fainted, and requested for himself that he might die, and said, “It is better for me to die than to live.”
verses.9:
God said to Jonah, “Is it right for you to be angry about the vine?”
He said, “I am right to be angry, even to death.”
verses.10: Yahweh said, “You have been concerned for the vine, for which you have not labored, neither made it grow; which came up in a night, and perished in a night.
verses.11: Shouldn’t I be concerned for Nineveh, that great city, in which are more than one hundred twenty thousand persons who can’t discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much livestock?”

verses.1: Yahweh’s word that came to Micah the Morashtite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
verses.2:
Hear, you peoples, all of you.
Listen, O earth, and all that is therein:
and let the Lord Yahweh be witness against you,
the Lord from his holy temple.
verses.3:
For, behold, Yahweh comes out of his place,
and will come down and tread on the high places of the earth.
verses.4:
The mountains melt under him,
and the valleys split apart,
like wax before the fire,
like waters that are poured down a steep place.
verses.5:
“All this is for the disobedience of Jacob,
and for the sins of the house of Israel.
What is the disobedience of Jacob?
Isn’t it Samaria?
And what are the high places of Judah?
Aren’t they Jerusalem?
verses.6:
Therefore I will make Samaria like a rubble heap of the field,
like places for planting vineyards;
and I will pour down its stones into the valley,
and I will uncover its foundations.
verses.9:
For her wounds are incurable;
for it has come even to Judah.
It reaches to the gate of my people,
even to Jerusalem.
verses.10:
Don’t tell it in Gath.
Don’t weep at all.
At Beth Ophrah I have rolled myself in the dust.
verses.11:
Pass on, inhabitant of Shaphir, in nakedness and shame.
The inhabitant of Zaanan won’t come out.
The wailing of Beth Ezel will take from you his protection.
verses.12:
For the inhabitant of Maroth waits anxiously for good,
because evil has come down from Yahweh to the gate of Jerusalem.
verses.14:
Therefore you will give a parting gift to Moresheth Gath.
The houses of Achzib will be a deceitful thing to the kings of Israel.
verses.15:
I will yet bring to you, inhabitant of Mareshah.
He who is the glory of Israel will come to Adullam.
verses.16:
Shave your heads,
and cut off your hair for the children of your delight.
Enlarge your baldness like the vulture;
for they have gone into captivity from you!

verses.1:
Woe to those who devise iniquity
and work evil on their beds!
When the morning is light, they practice it,
because it is in the power of their hand.
verses.2:
They covet fields, and seize them;
and houses, and take them away:
and they oppress a man and his house,
even a man and his heritage.
verses.4:
In that day they will take up a parable against you,
and lament with a doleful lamentation, saying,
‘We are utterly ruined!
My people’s possession is divided up.
Indeed he takes it from me and assigns our fields to traitors!’”
verses.5: Therefore you will have no one who divides the land by lot in Yahweh’s assembly.
verses.6:
“Don’t prophesy!”
They prophesy.
“Don’t prophesy about these things.
Disgrace won’t overtake us.”
verses.7:
Shall it be said, O house of Jacob:
“Is Yahweh’s Spirit angry?
Are these his doings?
Don’t my words do good to him who walks blamelessly?”
verses.8:
But lately my people have risen up as an enemy.
You strip the robe and clothing from those who pass by without a care, returning from battle.
verses.9:
You drive the women of my people out from their pleasant houses;
from their young children you take away my blessing forever.
verses.10:
Arise, and depart!
For this is not your resting place,
because of uncleanness that destroys,
even with a grievous destruction.
verses.13:
He who breaks open the way goes up before them.
They break through the gate, and go out.
And their king passes on before them,
with Yahweh at their head.

verses.1:
I said,
“Please listen, you heads of Jacob,
and rulers of the house of Israel:
Isn’t it for you to know justice?
verses.3:
who also eat the flesh of my people,
and flay their skin from off them,
and break their bones,
and chop them in pieces, as for the pot,
and as meat within the cauldron.
verses.4:
Then they will cry to Yahweh,
but he will not answer them.
Yes, he will hide his face from them at that time,
because they made their deeds evil.”
verses.5: Yahweh says concerning the prophets who lead my people astray; for those who feed their teeth, they proclaim, “Peace!” and whoever doesn’t provide for their mouths, they prepare war against him:
verses.6:
“Therefore night is over you, with no vision,
and it is dark to you, that you may not divine;
and the sun will go down on the prophets,
and the day will be black over them.
verses.7:
The seers shall be disappointed,
and the diviners confounded.
Yes, they shall all cover their lips;
for there is no answer from God.”
verses.8:
But as for me, I am full of power by Yahweh’s Spirit,
and of judgment, and of might,
to declare to Jacob his disobedience,
and to Israel his sin.
verses.9:
Please listen to this, you heads of the house of Jacob,
and rulers of the house of Israel,
who abhor justice,
and pervert all equity.
verses.10:
They build up Zion with blood,
and Jerusalem with iniquity.
verses.11:
Her leaders judge for bribes,
and her priests teach for a price,
and her prophets of it tell fortunes for money:
yet they lean on Yahweh, and say,
“Isn’t Yahweh among us?
No disaster will come on us.”
verses.12:
Therefore Zion for your sake will be plowed like a field,
and Jerusalem will become heaps of rubble,
and the mountain of the temple like the high places of a forest.

verses.1:
But in the latter days,
it will happen that the mountain of Yahweh’s temple will be established on the top of the mountains,
and it will be exalted above the hills;
and peoples will stream to it.
verses.2:
Many nations will go and say,
“Come, and let us go up to the mountain of Yahweh,
and to the house of the God of Jacob;
and he will teach us of his ways,
and we will walk in his paths.”
For the law will go out of Zion,
and Yahweh’s word from Jerusalem;
verses.3:
and he will judge between many peoples,
and will decide concerning strong nations afar off.
They will beat their swords into plowshares,
and their spears into pruning hooks.
Nation will not lift up sword against nation,
neither will they learn war any more.
verses.5:
Indeed all the nations may walk in the name of their gods;
but we will walk in the name of Yahweh our God forever and ever.
verses.6:
“In that day,” says Yahweh,
“I will assemble that which is lame,
and I will gather that which is driven away,
and that which I have afflicted;
verses.7:
and I will make that which was lame a remnant,
and that which was cast far off a strong nation:
and Yahweh will reign over them on Mount Zion from then on, even forever.”
verses.8:
You, tower of the flock, the hill of the daughter of Zion,
to you it will come,
yes, the former dominion will come,
the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.
verses.9:
Now why do you cry out aloud?
Is there no king in you?
Has your counselor perished,
that pains have taken hold of you as of a woman in travail?
verses.10:
Be in pain, and labor to give birth, daughter of Zion,
like a woman in travail;
for now you will go out of the city,
and will dwell in the field,
and will come even to Babylon.
There you will be rescued.
There Yahweh will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
verses.11:
Now many nations have assembled against you, that say,
“Let her be defiled,
and let our eye gloat over Zion.”

verses.1:
Now you shall gather yourself in troops,
daughter of troops.
He has laid siege against us.
They will strike the judge of Israel with a rod on the cheek.
verses.2:
But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah,
being small among the clans of Judah,
out of you one will come out to me that is to be ruler in Israel;
whose goings out are from of old, from ancient times.
verses.3:
Therefore he will abandon them until the time that she who is in labor gives birth.
Then the rest of his brothers will return to the children of Israel.
verses.4:
He shall stand, and shall shepherd in the strength of Yahweh,
in the majesty of the name of Yahweh his God:
and they will live, for then he will be great to the ends of the earth.
verses.5:
He will be our peace when Assyria invades our land,
and when he marches through our fortresses,
then we will raise against him seven shepherds,
and eight leaders of men.
verses.6:
They will rule the land of Assyria with the sword,
and the land of Nimrod in its gates.
He will deliver us from the Assyrian,
when he invades our land,
and when he marches within our border.
verses.7:
The remnant of Jacob will be among many peoples,
like dew from Yahweh,
like showers on the grass,
that don’t wait for man,
nor wait for the sons of men.
verses.8:
The remnant of Jacob will be among the nations,
among many peoples,
like a lion among the animals of the forest,
like a young lion among the flocks of sheep;
who, if he goes through, treads down and tears in pieces,
and there is no one to deliver.
verses.9:
Let your hand be lifted up above your adversaries,
and let all of your enemies be cut off.
verses.10:
“It will happen in that day”, says Yahweh,
“that I will cut off your horses out from among you,
and will destroy your chariots.
verses.11:
I will cut off the cities of your land,
and will tear down all your strongholds.
verses.12:
I will destroy witchcraft from your hand;
and you shall have no soothsayers.
verses.13:
I will cut off your engraved images and your pillars out from among you;
and you shall no more worship the work of your hands.
verses.14:
I will uproot your Asherah poles out from among you;
and I will destroy your cities.
verses.15:
I will execute vengeance in anger,
and wrath on the nations that didn’t listen.”

verses.1: Soon afterwards, he went about through cities and villages, preaching and bringing the good news of God’s Kingdom. With him were the twelve,
verses.2: and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary who was called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out;
verses.3: and Joanna, the wife of Chuzas, Herod’s steward; Susanna; and many others; who served them from their possessions.
verses.4: When a great multitude came together, and people from every city were coming to him, he spoke by a parable.
verses.5: “The farmer went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the road, and it was trampled under foot, and the birds of the sky devoured it.
verses.6: Other seed fell on the rock, and as soon as it grew, it withered away, because it had no moisture.
verses.7: Other fell amid the thorns, and the thorns grew with it, and choked it.
verses.8:
Other fell into the good ground, and grew, and produced one hundred times as much fruit.” As he said these things, he called out,
“He who has ears to hear, let him hear!”
verses.9: Then his disciples asked him, “What does this parable mean?”
verses.10:
He said,
“To you it is given to know the mysteries of God’s Kingdom, but to the rest in parables; that ‘seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.’
verses.11: Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
verses.12: Those along the road are those who hear, then the devil comes, and takes away the word from their heart, that they may not believe and be saved.
verses.13: Those on the rock are they who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; but these have no root, who believe for a while, then fall away in time of temptation.
verses.14: That which fell among the thorns, these are those who have heard, and as they go on their way they are choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of life, and bring no fruit to maturity.
verses.15: Those in the good ground, these are those who with an honest and good heart, having heard the word, hold it tightly, and produce fruit with perseverance.
verses.16: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, covers it with a container, or puts it under a bed; but puts it on a stand, that those who enter in may see the light.
verses.17: For nothing is hidden, that will not be revealed; nor anything secret, that will not be known and come to light.
verses.18: Be careful therefore how you hear. For whoever has, to him will be given; and whoever doesn’t have, from him will be taken away even that which he thinks he has.”
verses.19: His mother and brothers came to him, and they could not come near him for the crowd.
verses.20: Some people told him, “Your mother and your brothers stand outside, desiring to see you.”
verses.21:
But he answered them,
“My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God, and do it.”
verses.22:
Now on one of those days, he entered into a boat, himself and his disciples, and he said to them,
“Let’s go over to the other side of the lake.” So they launched out.
verses.23: But as they sailed, he fell asleep. A wind storm came down on the lake, and they were taking on dangerous amounts of water.
verses.24: They came to him, and awoke him, saying, “Master, master, we are dying!” He awoke, and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water, and they ceased, and it was calm.
verses.25:
He said to them,
“Where is your faith?” Being afraid they marveled, saying to one another, “Who is this then, that he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him?”
verses.26: They arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is opposite Galilee.
verses.27: When Jesus stepped ashore, a certain man out of the city who had demons for a long time met him. He wore no clothes, and didn’t live in a house, but in the tombs.
verses.28: When he saw Jesus, he cried out, and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, “What do I have to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I beg you, don’t torment me!”
verses.29: For Jesus was commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For the unclean spirit had often seized the man. He was kept under guard, and bound with chains and fetters. Breaking the bonds apart, he was driven by the demon into the desert.
verses.30:
Jesus asked him,
“What is your name?”
He said, “Legion,” for many demons had entered into him.
verses.31: They begged him that he would not command them to go into the abyss.
verses.32: Now there was there a herd of many pigs feeding on the mountain, and they begged him that he would allow them to enter into those. He allowed them.
verses.33: The demons came out of the man, and entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake, and were drowned.
verses.34: When those who fed them saw what had happened, they fled, and told it in the city and in the country.
verses.35: People went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus, and found the man from whom the demons had gone out, sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
verses.36: Those who saw it told them how he who had been possessed by demons was healed.
verses.37: All the people of the surrounding country of the Gadarenes asked him to depart from them, for they were very much afraid. He entered into the boat, and returned.
verses.38: But the man from whom the demons had gone out begged him that he might go with him, but Jesus sent him away, saying,
verses.39: “Return to your house, and declare what great things God has done for you.” He went his way, proclaiming throughout the whole city what great things Jesus had done for him.
verses.40: When Jesus returned, the multitude welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him.
verses.41: Behold, there came a man named Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue. He fell down at Jesus’ feet, and begged him to come into his house,
verses.42: for he had an only daughter, about twelve years of age, and she was dying. But as he went, the multitudes pressed against him.
verses.43: A woman who had a flow of blood for twelve years, who had spent all her living on physicians, and could not be healed by any,
verses.44: came behind him, and touched the fringe of his cloak, and immediately the flow of her blood stopped.
verses.45:
Jesus said,
“Who touched me?”
When all denied it, Peter and those with him said, “Master, the multitudes press and jostle you, and you say,
‘Who touched me?’”
verses.46:
But Jesus said,
“Someone did touch me, for I perceived that power has gone out of me.”
verses.47: When the woman saw that she was not hidden, she came trembling, and falling down before him declared to him in the presence of all the people the reason why she had touched him, and how she was healed immediately.
verses.48:
He said to her,
“Daughter, cheer up. Your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”
verses.49: While he still spoke, one from the ruler of the synagogue’s house came, saying to him, “Your daughter is dead. Don’t trouble the Teacher.”
verses.50:
But Jesus hearing it, answered him,
“Don’t be afraid. Only believe, and she will be healed.”
verses.51: When he came to the house, he didn’t allow anyone to enter in, except Peter, John, James, the father of the child, and her mother.
verses.52:
All were weeping and mourning her, but he said,
“Don’t weep. She isn’t dead, but sleeping.”
verses.53: They were ridiculing him, knowing that she was dead.
verses.54:
But he put them all outside, and taking her by the hand, he called, saying,
“Child, arise!”
verses.55: Her spirit returned, and she rose up immediately. He commanded that something be given to her to eat.
verses.56: Her parents were amazed, but he commanded them to tell no one what had been done.

verses.1: He called the twelve together, and gave them power and authority over all demons, and to cure diseases.
verses.2: He sent them out to preach God’s Kingdom and to heal the sick.
verses.3:
He said to them,
“Take nothing for your journey—neither staffs, nor wallet, nor bread, nor money; neither have two coats each.
verses.4: Into whatever house you enter, stay there, and depart from there.
verses.5: As many as don’t receive you, when you depart from that city, shake off even the dust from your feet for a testimony against them.”
verses.6: They departed, and went throughout the villages, preaching the Good News, and healing everywhere.
verses.7: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done by him; and he was very perplexed, because it was said by some that John had risen from the dead,
verses.8: and by some that Elijah had appeared, and by others that one of the old prophets had risen again.
verses.9: Herod said, “John I beheaded, but who is this, about whom I hear such things?” He sought to see him.
verses.10:
The apostles, when they had returned, told him what things they had done.
He took them, and withdrew apart to a desert region of a city called Bethsaida.
verses.11: But the multitudes, perceiving it, followed him. He welcomed them, and spoke to them of God’s Kingdom, and he cured those who needed healing.
verses.12: The day began to wear away; and the twelve came, and said to him, “Send the multitude away, that they may go into the surrounding villages and farms, and lodge, and get food, for we are here in a deserted place.”
verses.13:
But he said to them,
“You give them something to eat.”
They said, “We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we should go and buy food for all these people.”
verses.14:
For they were about five thousand men.
He said to his disciples,
“Make them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”
verses.15: They did so, and made them all sit down.
verses.16: He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to the sky, he blessed them, and broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the multitude.
verses.17: They ate, and were all filled. They gathered up twelve baskets of broken pieces that were left over.
verses.18:
As he was praying alone, the disciples were with him, and he asked them,
“Who do the multitudes say that I am?”
verses.19: They answered, “‘John the Baptizer,’ but others say, ‘Elijah,’ and others, that one of the old prophets is risen again.”
verses.20:
He said to them,
“But who do you say that I am?”
Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”
verses.21: But he warned them, and commanded them to tell this to no one,
verses.22:
saying,
“The Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.”
verses.23:
He said to all,
“If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross,
and follow me.
verses.24: For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, but whoever will lose his life for my sake, the same will save it.
verses.25: For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world, and loses or forfeits his own self?
verses.26: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words, of him will the Son of Man be ashamed, when he comes in his glory, and the glory of the Father, and of the holy angels.
verses.27: But I tell you the truth: There are some of those who stand here, who will in no way taste of death, until they see God’s Kingdom.”
verses.28: About eight days after these sayings, he took with him Peter, John, and James, and went up onto the mountain to pray.
verses.29: As he was praying, the appearance of his face was altered, and his clothing became white and dazzling.
verses.30: Behold, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,
verses.31: who appeared in glory, and spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.
verses.32: Now Peter and those who were with him were heavy with sleep, but when they were fully awake, they saw his glory, and the two men who stood with him.
verses.33: As they were parting from him, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let’s make three tents: one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah,” not knowing what he said.
verses.34: While he said these things, a cloud came and overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered into the cloud.
verses.35: A voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!”
verses.36: When the voice came, Jesus was found alone. They were silent, and told no one in those days any of the things which they had seen.
verses.37: On the next day, when they had come down from the mountain, a great multitude met him.
verses.38: Behold, a man from the crowd called out, saying, “Teacher, I beg you to look at my son, for he is my only child.
verses.39: Behold, a spirit takes him, he suddenly cries out, and it convulses him so that he foams, and it hardly departs from him, bruising him severely.
verses.40: I begged your disciples to cast it out, and they couldn’t.”
verses.41:
Jesus answered,
“Faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here.”
verses.42: While he was still coming, the demon threw him down and convulsed him violently. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
verses.43:
They were all astonished at the majesty of God.
But while all were marveling at all the things which Jesus did, he said to his disciples,
verses.44: “Let these words sink into your ears, for the Son of Man will be delivered up into the hands of men.”
verses.45: But they didn’t understand this saying. It was concealed from them, that they should not perceive it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.
verses.46: There arose an argument among them about which of them was the greatest.
verses.47: Jesus, perceiving the reasoning of their hearts, took a little child, and set him by his side,
verses.48:
and said to them,
“Whoever receives this little child in my name receives me. Whoever receives me receives him who sent me. For whoever is least among you all, this one will be great.”
verses.49: John answered, “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we forbade him, because he doesn’t follow with us.”
verses.50:
Jesus said to him,
“Don’t forbid him, for he who is not against us is for us.”
verses.51: It came to pass, when the days were near that he should be taken up, he intently set his face to go to Jerusalem,
verses.52: and sent messengers before his face. They went, and entered into a village of the Samaritans, so as to prepare for him.
verses.53: They didn’t receive him, because he was traveling with his face set towards Jerusalem.
verses.54: When his disciples, James and John, saw this, they said, “Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from the sky, and destroy them, just as Elijah did?”
verses.55:
But he turned and rebuked them,
“You don’t know of what kind of spirit you are.
verses.56:
For the Son of Man didn’t come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them.”
They went to another village.
verses.57: As they went on the way, a certain man said to him, “I want to follow you wherever you go, Lord.”
verses.58:
Jesus said to him,
“The foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay his head.”
verses.59:
He said to another,
“Follow me!”
But he said, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”
verses.60:
But Jesus said to him,
“Leave the dead to bury their own dead, but you go and announce God’s Kingdom.”
verses.61: Another also said, “I want to follow you, Lord, but first allow me to say good-bye to those who are at my house.”
verses.62:
But Jesus said to him,
“No one, having put his hand to the plow, and looking back, is fit for God’s Kingdom.”

verses.1: Now after these things, the Lord also appointed seventy others, and sent them two by two ahead of him into every city and place, where he was about to come.
verses.2:
Then he said to them,
“The harvest is indeed plentiful, but the laborers are few. Pray therefore to the Lord of the harvest, that he may send out laborers into his harvest.
verses.3: Go your ways. Behold, I send you out as lambs among wolves.
verses.4: Carry no purse, nor wallet, nor sandals. Greet no one on the way.
verses.5: Into whatever house you enter, first say, ‘Peace be to this house.’
verses.6: If a son of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; but if not, it will return to you.
verses.7: Remain in that same house, eating and drinking the things they give, for the laborer is worthy of his wages. Don’t go from house to house.
verses.8: Into whatever city you enter, and they receive you, eat the things that are set before you.
verses.9: Heal the sick who are therein, and tell them, ‘God’s Kingdom has come near to you.’
verses.10: But into whatever city you enter, and they don’t receive you, go out into its streets and say,
verses.11: ‘Even the dust from your city that clings to us, we wipe off against you. Nevertheless know this, that God’s Kingdom has come near to you.’
verses.12: I tell you, it will be more tolerable in that day for Sodom than for that city.
verses.13: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
verses.14: But it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment than for you.
verses.15: You, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, will be brought down to Hades.
verses.16: Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me. Whoever rejects me rejects him who sent me.”
verses.17: The seventy returned with joy, saying, “Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!”
verses.18:
He said to them,
“I saw Satan having fallen like lightning from heaven.
verses.19: Behold, I give you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will in any way hurt you.
verses.20: Nevertheless, don’t rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”
verses.21:
In that same hour Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit, and said,
“I thank you, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in your sight.”
verses.22:
Turning to the disciples, he said,
“All things have been delivered to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is, except the Father, and who the Father is, except the Son, and he to whomever the Son desires to reveal him.”
verses.23:
Turning to the disciples, he said privately,
“Blessed are the eyes which see the things that you see,
verses.24: for I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see the things which you see, and didn’t see them, and to hear the things which you hear, and didn’t hear them.”
verses.25: Behold, a certain lawyer stood up and tested him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
verses.26:
He said to him,
“What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
verses.27: He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself.”
verses.28:
He said to him,
“You have answered correctly. Do this, and you will live.”
verses.29: But he, desiring to justify himself, asked Jesus, “Who is my neighbor?”
verses.30:
Jesus answered,
“A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
verses.31: By chance a certain priest was going down that way. When he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
verses.32: In the same way a Levite also, when he came to the place, and saw him, passed by on the other side.
verses.33: But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion,
verses.34: came to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
verses.35: On the next day, when he departed, he took out two denarii, and gave them to the host, and said to him, ‘Take care of him. Whatever you spend beyond that, I will repay you when I return.’
verses.36: Now which of these three do you think seemed to be a neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?”
verses.37:
He said, “He who showed mercy on him.”
Then Jesus said to him,
“Go and do likewise.”
verses.38: As they went on their way, he entered into a certain village, and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.
verses.39: She had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word.
verses.40: But Martha was distracted with much serving, and she came up to him, and said, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Ask her therefore to help me.”
verses.41:
Jesus answered her,
“Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,
verses.42: but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”

verses.1: When he finished praying in a certain place, one of his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”
verses.2:
He said to them,
“When you pray, say,
‘Our Father in heaven,
may your name be kept holy.
May your Kingdom come.
May your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.
verses.3: Give us day by day our daily bread.
verses.4:
Forgive us our sins,
for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is indebted to us.

Bring us not into temptation,
but deliver us from the evil one.’”
verses.5:
He said to them,
“Which of you, if you go to a friend at midnight, and tell him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
verses.6: for a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him,’
verses.7: and he from within will answer and say, ‘Don’t bother me. The door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed. I can’t get up and give it to you’?
verses.8: I tell you, although he will not rise and give it to him because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence, he will get up and give him as many as he needs.
verses.9: “I tell you, keep asking, and it will be given you. Keep seeking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and it will be opened to you.
verses.10: For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.
verses.11: “Which of you fathers, if your son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, he won’t give him a snake instead of a fish, will he?
verses.12: Or if he asks for an egg, he won’t give him a scorpion, will he?
verses.13: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?”
verses.14: He was casting out a demon, and it was mute. When the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke; and the multitudes marveled.
verses.15: But some of them said, “He casts out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons.”
verses.16: Others, testing him, sought from him a sign from heaven.
verses.17:
But he, knowing their thoughts, said to them,
“Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. A house divided against itself falls.
verses.18: If Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out demons by Beelzebul.
verses.19: But if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your children cast them out? Therefore will they be your judges.
verses.20: But if I by God’s finger cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come to you.
verses.21: “When the strong man, fully armed, guards his own dwelling, his goods are safe.
verses.22: But when someone stronger attacks him and overcomes him, he takes from him his whole armor in which he trusted, and divides his plunder.
verses.23: “He that is not with me is against me. He who doesn’t gather with me scatters.
verses.24: The unclean spirit, when he has gone out of the man, passes through dry places, seeking rest, and finding none, he says, ‘I will turn back to my house from which I came out.’
verses.25: When he returns, he finds it swept and put in order.
verses.26: Then he goes, and takes seven other spirits more evil than himself, and they enter in and dwell there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first.”
verses.27: It came to pass, as he said these things, a certain woman out of the multitude lifted up her voice, and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts which nursed you!”
verses.28:
But he said,
“On the contrary, blessed are those who hear the word of God, and keep it.”
verses.29:
When the multitudes were gathering together to him, he began to say,
“This is an evil generation. It seeks after a sign. No sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah, the prophet.
verses.30: For even as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so will also the Son of Man be to this generation.
verses.31: The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and will condemn them: for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here.
verses.32: The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold, one greater than Jonah is here.
verses.33: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, puts it in a cellar or under a basket, but on a stand, that those who come in may see the light.
verses.34: The lamp of the body is the eye. Therefore when your eye is good, your whole body is also full of light; but when it is evil, your body also is full of darkness.
verses.35: Therefore see whether the light that is in you isn’t darkness.
verses.36: If therefore your whole body is full of light, having no part dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when the lamp with its bright shining gives you light.”
verses.37: Now as he spoke, a certain Pharisee asked him to dine with him. He went in, and sat at the table.
verses.38: When the Pharisee saw it, he marveled that he had not first washed himself before dinner.
verses.39:
The Lord said to him,
“Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but your inward part is full of extortion and wickedness.
verses.40: You foolish ones, didn’t he who made the outside make the inside also?
verses.41: But give for gifts to the needy those things which are within, and behold, all things will be clean to you.
verses.42: But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every herb, but you bypass justice and God’s love. You ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.
verses.43: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the best seats in the synagogues, and the greetings in the marketplaces.
verses.44: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like hidden graves, and the men who walk over them don’t know it.”
verses.45: One of the lawyers answered him, “Teacher, in saying this you insult us also.”
verses.46:
He said,
“Woe to you lawyers also! For you load men with burdens that are difficult to carry, and you yourselves won’t even lift one finger to help carry those burdens.
verses.47: Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
verses.48: So you testify and consent to the works of your fathers. For they killed them, and you build their tombs.
verses.49: Therefore also the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send to them prophets and apostles; and some of them they will kill and persecute,
verses.50: that the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;
verses.51: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zachariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary.’ Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation.
verses.52: Woe to you lawyers! For you took away the key of knowledge. You didn’t enter in yourselves, and those who were entering in, you hindered.”
verses.53: As he said these things to them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to be terribly angry, and to draw many things out of him;
verses.54: lying in wait for him, and seeking to catch him in something he might say, that they might accuse him.

verses.1:
Meanwhile, when a multitude of many thousands had gathered together, so much so that they trampled on each other, he began to tell his disciples first of all,
“Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
verses.2: But there is nothing covered up, that will not be revealed, nor hidden, that will not be known.
verses.3: Therefore whatever you have said in the darkness will be heard in the light. What you have spoken in the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.
verses.4: “I tell you, my friends, don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.
verses.5:
But I will warn you whom you should fear. Fear him, who after he has killed, has power to cast into Gehenna.
Yes, I tell you, fear him.
verses.6: “Aren’t five sparrows sold for two assaria coins? Not one of them is forgotten by God.
verses.7: But the very hairs of your head are all counted. Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.
verses.8: “I tell you, everyone who confesses me before men, him will the Son of Man also confess before the angels of God;
verses.9: but he who denies me in the presence of men will be denied in the presence of the angels of God.
verses.10: Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but those who blaspheme against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
verses.11: When they bring you before the synagogues, the rulers, and the authorities, don’t be anxious how or what you will answer, or what you will say;
verses.12: for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that same hour what you must say.”
verses.13: One of the multitude said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
verses.14:
But he said to him,
“Man, who made me a judge or an arbitrator over you?”
verses.15:
He said to them,
“Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”
verses.16:
He spoke a parable to them, saying,
“The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly.
verses.17: He reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What will I do, because I don’t have room to store my crops?’
verses.18: He said, ‘This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns, and build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
verses.19: I will tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease, eat, drink, be merry.”’
verses.20: “But God said to him, ‘You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared—whose will they be?’
verses.21: So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.”
verses.22:
He said to his disciples,
“Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life, what you will eat, nor yet for your body, what you will wear.
verses.23: Life is more than food, and the body is more than clothing.
verses.24: Consider the ravens: they don’t sow, they don’t reap, they have no warehouse or barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds!
verses.25: Which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his height?
verses.26: If then you aren’t able to do even the least things, why are you anxious about the rest?
verses.27: Consider the lilies, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin; yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
verses.28: But if this is how God clothes the grass in the field, which today exists, and tomorrow is cast into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith?
verses.29: Don’t seek what you will eat or what you will drink; neither be anxious.
verses.30: For the nations of the world seek after all of these things, but your Father knows that you need these things.
verses.31: But seek God’s Kingdom, and all these things will be added to you.
verses.32: Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.
verses.33: Sell that which you have, and give gifts to the needy. Make for yourselves purses which don’t grow old, a treasure in the heavens that doesn’t fail, where no thief approaches, neither moth destroys.
verses.34: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
verses.35: “Let your waist be dressed and your lamps burning.
verses.36: Be like men watching for their lord, when he returns from the marriage feast; that, when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open to him.
verses.37: Blessed are those servants, whom the lord will find watching when he comes. Most certainly I tell you, that he will dress himself, and make them recline, and will come and serve them.
verses.38: They will be blessed if he comes in the second or third watch, and finds them so.
verses.39: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would have watched, and not allowed his house to be broken into.
verses.40: Therefore be ready also, for the Son of Man is coming in an hour that you don’t expect him.”
verses.41: Peter said to him, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everybody?”
verses.42:
The Lord said,
“Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his lord will set over his household, to give them their portion of food at the right times?
verses.43: Blessed is that servant whom his lord will find doing so when he comes.
verses.44: Truly I tell you, that he will set him over all that he has.
verses.45: But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My lord delays his coming,’ and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken,
verses.46: then the lord of that servant will come in a day when he isn’t expecting him, and in an hour that he doesn’t know, and will cut him in two, and place his portion with the unfaithful.
verses.47: That servant, who knew his lord’s will, and didn’t prepare, nor do what he wanted, will be beaten with many stripes,
verses.48: but he who didn’t know, and did things worthy of stripes, will be beaten with few stripes. To whomever much is given, of him will much be required; and to whom much was entrusted, of him more will be asked.
verses.49: “I came to throw fire on the earth. I wish it were already kindled.
verses.50: But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
verses.51: Do you think that I have come to give peace in the earth? I tell you, no, but rather division.
verses.52: For from now on, there will be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.
verses.53: They will be divided, father against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”
verses.54: He said to the multitudes also, “When you see a cloud rising from the west, immediately you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and so it happens.
verses.55: When a south wind blows, you say, ‘There will be a scorching heat,’ and it happens.
verses.56: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you don’t interpret this time?
verses.57: Why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?
verses.58: For when you are going with your adversary before the magistrate, try diligently on the way to be released from him, lest perhaps he drag you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
verses.59: I tell you, you will by no means get out of there, until you have paid the very last penny.”

verses.1: Now there were some present at the same time who told him about the Galileans, whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
verses.2:
Jesus answered them,
“Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered such things?
verses.3: I tell you, no, but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
verses.4: Or those eighteen, on whom the tower in Siloam fell, and killed them; do you think that they were worse offenders than all the men who dwell in Jerusalem?
verses.5: I tell you, no, but, unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.”
verses.6:
He spoke this parable.
“A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it, and found none.
verses.7: He said to the vine dresser, ‘Behold, these three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and found none. Cut it down. Why does it waste the soil?’
verses.8: He answered, ‘Lord, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it, and fertilize it.
verses.9: If it bears fruit, fine; but if not, after that, you can cut it down.’”
verses.10: He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath day.
verses.11: Behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and she was bent over, and could in no way straighten herself up.
verses.12:
When Jesus saw her, he called her, and said to her,
“Woman, you are freed from your infirmity.”
verses.13: He laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight, and glorified God.
verses.14: The ruler of the synagogue, being indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, said to the multitude, “There are six days in which men ought to work. Therefore come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day!”
verses.15:
Therefore the Lord answered him,
“You hypocrites! Doesn’t each one of you free his ox or his donkey from the stall on the Sabbath, and lead him away to water?
verses.16: Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan had bound eighteen long years, be freed from this bondage on the Sabbath day?”
verses.17: As he said these things, all his adversaries were disappointed, and all the multitude rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.
verses.18:
He said,
“What is God’s Kingdom like? To what shall I compare it?
verses.19: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and put in his own garden. It grew, and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky live in its branches.”
verses.20:
Again he said,
“To what shall I compare God’s Kingdom?
verses.21:
It is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures

of flour, until it was all leavened.”
verses.22: He went on his way through cities and villages, teaching, and traveling on to Jerusalem.
verses.23:
One said to him, “Lord, are they few who are saved?”
He said to them,
verses.24: “Strive to enter in by the narrow door, for many, I tell you, will seek to enter in, and will not be able.
verses.25: When once the master of the house has risen up, and has shut the door, and you begin to stand outside, and to knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us!’ then he will answer and tell you, ‘I don’t know you or where you come from.’
verses.26: Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’
verses.27: He will say, ‘I tell you, I don’t know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.’
verses.28: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets, in God’s Kingdom, and yourselves being thrown outside.
verses.29: They will come from the east, west, north, and south, and will sit down in God’s Kingdom.
verses.30: Behold, there are some who are last who will be first, and there are some who are first who will be last.”
verses.31: On that same day, some Pharisees came, saying to him, “Get out of here, and go away, for Herod wants to kill you.”
verses.32:
He said to them,
“Go and tell that fox, ‘Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I complete my mission.
verses.33: Nevertheless I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the next day, for it can’t be that a prophet would perish outside of Jerusalem.’
verses.34: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that kills the prophets, and stones those who are sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together, like a hen gathers her own brood under her wings, and you refused!
verses.35: Behold, your house is left to you desolate. I tell you, you will not see me, until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”

verses.1: When he went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him.
verses.2: Behold, a certain man who had dropsy was in front of him.
verses.3:
Jesus, answering, spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying,
“Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”
verses.4:
But they were silent.
He took him, and healed him, and let him go.
verses.5:
He answered them,
“Which of you, if your son
or an ox fell into a well, wouldn’t immediately pull him out on a Sabbath day?”
verses.6: They couldn’t answer him regarding these things.
verses.7: He spoke a parable to those who were invited, when he noticed how they chose the best seats, and said to them,
verses.8: “When you are invited by anyone to a marriage feast, don’t sit in the best seat, since perhaps someone more honorable than you might be invited by him,
verses.9: and he who invited both of you would come and tell you, ‘Make room for this person.’ Then you would begin, with shame, to take the lowest place.
verses.10: But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes, he may tell you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all who sit at the table with you.
verses.11: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
verses.12:
He also said to the one who had invited him,
“When you make a dinner or a supper, don’t call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your kinsmen, nor rich neighbors, or perhaps they might also return the favor, and pay you back.
verses.13: But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind;
