verses.14: and you will be blessed, because they don’t have the resources to repay you. For you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous.”
verses.15: When one of those who sat at the table with him heard these things, he said to him, “Blessed is he who will feast in God’s Kingdom!”
verses.16:
But he said to him,
“A certain man made a great supper, and he invited many people.
verses.17: He sent out his servant at supper time to tell those who were invited, ‘Come, for everything is ready now.’
verses.18:
They all as one began to make excuses.
“The first said to him, ‘I have bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please have me excused.’
verses.19: “Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I must go try them out. Please have me excused.’
verses.20: “Another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I can’t come.’
verses.21: “That servant came, and told his lord these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor, maimed, blind, and lame.’
verses.22: “The servant said, ‘Lord, it is done as you commanded, and there is still room.’
verses.23: “The lord said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
verses.24: For I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste of my supper.’”
verses.25: Now great multitudes were going with him. He turned and said to them,
verses.26:
“If anyone comes to me, and doesn’t disregard
his own father, mother, wife, children, brothers, and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he can’t be my disciple.
verses.27: Whoever doesn’t bear his own cross, and come after me, can’t be my disciple.
verses.28: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?
verses.29: Or perhaps, when he has laid a foundation, and is not able to finish, everyone who sees begins to mock him,
verses.30: saying, ‘This man began to build, and wasn’t able to finish.’
verses.31: Or what king, as he goes to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?
verses.32: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends an envoy, and asks for conditions of peace.
verses.33: So therefore whoever of you who doesn’t renounce all that he has, he can’t be my disciple.
verses.34: Salt is good, but if the salt becomes flat and tasteless, with what do you season it?
verses.35: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile. It is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

verses.1: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were coming close to him to hear him.
verses.2: The Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them.”
verses.3: He told them this parable.
verses.4: “Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep, and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?
verses.5: When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
verses.6: When he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’
verses.7: I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.
verses.8:
Or what woman, if she had ten drachma
coins, if she lost one drachma coin, wouldn’t light a lamp, sweep the house, and seek diligently until she found it?
verses.9: When she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma which I had lost.’
verses.10: Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”
verses.11:
He said,
“A certain man had two sons.
verses.12: The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of your property.’ He divided his livelihood between them.
verses.13: Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.
verses.14: When he had spent all of it, there arose a severe famine in that country, and he began to be in need.
verses.15: He went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
verses.16: He wanted to fill his belly with the husks that the pigs ate, but no one gave him any.
verses.17: But when he came to himself he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!
verses.18: I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight.
verses.19: I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”’
verses.20: “He arose, and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
verses.21: The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
verses.22: “But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe, and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet.
verses.23: Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let us eat, and celebrate;
verses.24: for this, my son, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’ They began to celebrate.
verses.25: “Now his elder son was in the field. As he came near to the house, he heard music and dancing.
verses.26: He called one of the servants to him, and asked what was going on.
verses.27: He said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and healthy.’
verses.28: But he was angry, and would not go in. Therefore his father came out, and begged him.
verses.29: But he answered his father, ‘Behold, these many years I have served you, and I never disobeyed a commandment of yours, but you never gave me a goat, that I might celebrate with my friends.
verses.30: But when this your son came, who has devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.’
verses.31: “He said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
verses.32: But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, your brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’”

verses.1:
He also said to his disciples,
“There was a certain rich man who had a manager. An accusation was made to him that this man was wasting his possessions.
verses.2: He called him, and said to him, ‘What is this that I hear about you? Give an accounting of your management, for you can no longer be manager.’
verses.3: “The manager said within himself, ‘What will I do, seeing that my lord is taking away the management position from me? I don’t have strength to dig. I am ashamed to beg.
verses.4: I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from management, they may receive me into their houses.’
verses.5: Calling each one of his lord’s debtors to him, he said to the first, ‘How much do you owe to my lord?’
verses.6: He said, ‘A hundred batos of oil.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and sit down quickly and write fifty.’
verses.7: Then he said to another, ‘How much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and write eighty.’
verses.8: “His lord commended the dishonest manager because he had done wisely, for the children of this world are, in their own generation, wiser than the children of the light.
verses.9: I tell you, make for yourselves friends by means of unrighteous mammon, so that when you fail, they may receive you into the eternal tents.
verses.10: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
verses.11: If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?
verses.12: If you have not been faithful in that which is another’s, who will give you that which is your own?
verses.13: No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to one, and despise the other. You aren’t able to serve God and Mammon.”
verses.14: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, also heard all these things, and they scoffed at him.
verses.15:
He said to them,
“You are those who justify yourselves in the sight of men, but God knows your hearts. For that which is exalted among men is an abomination in the sight of God.
verses.16: The law and the prophets were until John. From that time the Good News of God’s Kingdom is preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
verses.17: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away, than for one tiny stroke of a pen in the law to fall.
verses.18: Everyone who divorces his wife, and marries another, commits adultery. He who marries one who is divorced from a husband commits adultery.
verses.19: “Now there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, living in luxury every day.
verses.20: A certain beggar, named Lazarus, was taken to his gate, full of sores,
verses.21: and desiring to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Yes, even the dogs came and licked his sores.
verses.22: The beggar died, and he was carried away by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died, and was buried.
verses.23: In Hades, he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and saw Abraham far off, and Lazarus at his bosom.
verses.24: He cried and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue! For I am in anguish in this flame.’
verses.25: “But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember that you, in your lifetime, received your good things, and Lazarus, in the same way, bad things. But here he is now comforted, and you are in anguish.
verses.26: Besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, that those who want to pass from here to you are not able, and that no one may cross over from there to us.’
verses.27: “He said, ‘I ask you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father’s house;
verses.28: for I have five brothers, that he may testify to them, so they won’t also come into this place of torment.’
verses.29: “But Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them.’
verses.30: “He said, ‘No, father Abraham, but if one goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’
verses.31: “He said to him, ‘If they don’t listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded if one rises from the dead.’”

verses.1:
He said to the disciples,
“It is impossible that no occasions of stumbling should come, but woe to him through whom they come!
verses.2: It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
verses.3: Be careful. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him.
verses.4: If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”
verses.5: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”
verses.6:
The Lord said,
“If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would tell this sycamore tree, ‘Be uprooted, and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.
verses.7: But who is there among you, having a servant plowing or keeping sheep, that will say, when he comes in from the field, ‘Come immediately and sit down at the table,’
verses.8: and will not rather tell him, ‘Prepare my supper, clothe yourself properly, and serve me, while I eat and drink. Afterward you shall eat and drink’?
verses.9: Does he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded? I think not.
verses.10: Even so you also, when you have done all the things that are commanded you, say, ‘We are unworthy servants. We have done our duty.’”
verses.11: As he was on his way to Jerusalem, he was passing along the borders of Samaria and Galilee.
verses.12: As he entered into a certain village, ten men who were lepers met him, who stood at a distance.
verses.13: They lifted up their voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
verses.14:
When he saw them, he said to them,
“Go and show yourselves to the priests.” As they went, they were cleansed.
verses.15: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.
verses.16: He fell on his face at Jesus’ feet, giving him thanks; and he was a Samaritan.
verses.17:
Jesus answered,
“Weren’t the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?
verses.18: Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this stranger?”
verses.19:
Then he said to him,
“Get up, and go your way. Your faith has healed you.”
verses.20:
Being asked by the Pharisees when God’s Kingdom would come, he answered them,
“God’s Kingdom doesn’t come with observation;
verses.21: neither will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ for behold, God’s Kingdom is within you.”
verses.22:
He said to the disciples,
“The days will come, when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
verses.23: They will tell you, ‘Look, here!’ or ‘Look, there!’ Don’t go away, nor follow after them,
verses.24: for as the lightning, when it flashes out of the one part under the sky, shines to the other part under the sky; so will the Son of Man be in his day.
verses.25: But first, he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
verses.26: As it was in the days of Noah, even so will it be also in the days of the Son of Man.
verses.27: They ate, they drank, they married, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ship, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.
verses.28: Likewise, even as it was in the days of Lot: they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built;
verses.29: but in the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from the sky, and destroyed them all.
verses.30: It will be the same way in the day that the Son of Man is revealed.
verses.31: In that day, he who will be on the housetop, and his goods in the house, let him not go down to take them away. Let him who is in the field likewise not turn back.
verses.32: Remember Lot’s wife!
verses.33: Whoever seeks to save his life loses it, but whoever loses his life preserves it.
verses.34: I tell you, in that night there will be two people in one bed. The one will be taken, and the other will be left.
verses.35: There will be two grinding grain together. One will be taken, and the other will be left.”
verses.37:
They, answering, asked him, “Where, Lord?”
He said to them,
“Where the body is, there will the vultures also be gathered together.”

verses.1: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray, and not give up,
verses.2:
saying,
“There was a judge in a certain city who didn’t fear God, and didn’t respect man.
verses.3: A widow was in that city, and she often came to him, saying, ‘Defend me from my adversary!’
verses.4: He wouldn’t for a while, but afterward he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God, nor respect man,
verses.5: yet because this widow bothers me, I will defend her, or else she will wear me out by her continual coming.’”
verses.6:
The Lord said,
“Listen to what the unrighteous judge says.
verses.7: Won’t God avenge his chosen ones, who are crying out to him day and night, and yet he exercises patience with them?
verses.8: I tell you that he will avenge them quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”
verses.9: He spoke also this parable to certain people who were convinced of their own righteousness, and who despised all others.
verses.10: “Two men went up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector.
verses.11: The Pharisee stood and prayed to himself like this: ‘God, I thank you, that I am not like the rest of men, extortionists, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
verses.12: I fast twice a week. I give tithes of all that I get.’
verses.13: But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’
verses.14: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.”
verses.15: They were also bringing their babies to him, that he might touch them. But when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
verses.16:
Jesus summoned them, saying,
“Allow the little children to come to me, and don’t hinder them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
verses.17: Most certainly, I tell you, whoever doesn’t receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”
verses.18: A certain ruler asked him, saying, “Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
verses.19:
Jesus asked him,
“Why do you call me good? No one is good, except one—God.
verses.20: You know the commandments: ‘Don’t commit adultery,’ ‘Don’t murder,’ ‘Don’t steal,’ ‘Don’t give false testimony,’ ‘Honor your father and your mother.’”
verses.21: He said, “I have observed all these things from my youth up.”
verses.22:
When Jesus heard these things, he said to him,
“You still lack one thing. Sell all that you have, and distribute it to the poor. You will have treasure in heaven. Come, follow me.”
verses.23: But when he heard these things, he became very sad, for he was very rich.
verses.24:
Jesus, seeing that he became very sad, said,
“How hard it is for those who have riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!
verses.25: For it is easier for a camel to enter in through a needle’s eye, than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”
verses.26: Those who heard it said, “Then who can be saved?”
verses.27:
But he said,
“The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.”
verses.28: Peter said, “Look, we have left everything, and followed you.”
verses.29:
He said to them,
“Most certainly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or wife, or brothers, or parents, or children, for God’s Kingdom’s sake,
verses.30: who will not receive many times more in this time, and in the world to come, eternal life.”
verses.31:
He took the twelve aside, and said to them,
“Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things that are written through the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be completed.
verses.32: For he will be delivered up to the Gentiles, will be mocked, treated shamefully, and spit on.
verses.33: They will scourge and kill him. On the third day, he will rise again.”
verses.34: They understood none of these things. This saying was hidden from them, and they didn’t understand the things that were said.
verses.35: As he came near Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the road, begging.
verses.36: Hearing a multitude going by, he asked what this meant.
verses.37: They told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.
verses.38: He cried out, “Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!”
verses.39: Those who led the way rebuked him, that he should be quiet; but he cried out all the more, “You son of David, have mercy on me!”
verses.40: Standing still, Jesus commanded him to be brought to him. When he had come near, he asked him,
verses.41:
“What do you want me to do?”
He said, “Lord, that I may see again.”
verses.42:
Jesus said to him,
“Receive your sight. Your faith has healed you.”
verses.43: Immediately he received his sight, and followed him, glorifying God. All the people, when they saw it, praised God.

verses.1: He entered and was passing through Jericho.
verses.2: There was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
verses.3: He was trying to see who Jesus was, and couldn’t because of the crowd, because he was short.
verses.4: He ran on ahead, and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was going to pass that way.
verses.5:
When Jesus came to the place, he looked up and saw him, and said to him,
“Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.”
verses.6: He hurried, came down, and received him joyfully.
verses.7: When they saw it, they all murmured, saying, “He has gone in to lodge with a man who is a sinner.”
verses.8: Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much.”
verses.9:
Jesus said to him,
“Today, salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.
verses.10: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”
verses.11: As they heard these things, he went on and told a parable, because he was near Jerusalem, and they supposed that God’s Kingdom would be revealed immediately.
verses.12:
He said therefore,
“A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.
verses.13:
He called ten servants of his, and gave them ten mina coins,

and told them, ‘Conduct business until I come.’
verses.14: But his citizens hated him, and sent an envoy after him, saying, ‘We don’t want this man to reign over us.’
verses.15: “When he had come back again, having received the kingdom, he commanded these servants, to whom he had given the money, to be called to him, that he might know what they had gained by conducting business.
verses.16: The first came before him, saying, ‘Lord, your mina has made ten more minas.’
verses.17: “He said to him, ‘Well done, you good servant! Because you were found faithful with very little, you shall have authority over ten cities.’
verses.18: “The second came, saying, ‘Your mina, Lord, has made five minas.’
verses.19: “So he said to him, ‘And you are to be over five cities.’
verses.20: Another came, saying, ‘Lord, behold, your mina, which I kept laid away in a handkerchief,
verses.21: for I feared you, because you are an exacting man. You take up that which you didn’t lay down, and reap that which you didn’t sow.’
verses.22: “He said to him, ‘Out of your own mouth will I judge you, you wicked servant! You knew that I am an exacting man, taking up that which I didn’t lay down, and reaping that which I didn’t sow.
verses.23: Then why didn’t you deposit my money in the bank, and at my coming, I might have earned interest on it?’
verses.24: He said to those who stood by, ‘Take the mina away from him, and give it to him who has the ten minas.’
verses.25: “They said to him, ‘Lord, he has ten minas!’
verses.26: ‘For I tell you that to everyone who has, will more be given; but from him who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away from him.
verses.27: But bring those enemies of mine who didn’t want me to reign over them here, and kill them before me.’”
verses.28: Having said these things, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
verses.29: When he came near to Bethsphage and Bethany, at the mountain that is called Olivet, he sent two of his disciples,
verses.30:
saying,
“Go your way into the village on the other side, in which, as you enter, you will find a colt tied, which no man had ever sat upon. Untie it, and bring it.
verses.31: If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ say to him: ‘The Lord needs it.’”
verses.32: Those who were sent went away, and found things just as he had told them.
verses.33: As they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, “Why are you untying the colt?”
verses.34: They said, “The Lord needs it.”
verses.35: They brought it to Jesus. They threw their cloaks on the colt, and set Jesus on them.
verses.36: As he went, they spread their cloaks on the road.
verses.37: As he was now getting near, at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works which they had seen,
verses.38:
saying, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!
 Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!”
verses.39: Some of the Pharisees from the multitude said to him, “Teacher, rebuke your disciples!”
verses.40:
He answered them,
“I tell you that if these were silent, the stones would cry out.”
verses.41: When he came near, he saw the city and wept over it,
verses.42:
saying,
“If you, even you, had known today the things which belong to your peace! But now, they are hidden from your eyes.
verses.43: For the days will come on you, when your enemies will throw up a barricade against you, surround you, hem you in on every side,
verses.44: and will dash you and your children within you to the ground. They will not leave in you one stone on another, because you didn’t know the time of your visitation.”
verses.45: He entered into the temple, and began to drive out those who bought and sold in it,
verses.46:
saying to them,
“It is written, ‘My house is a house of prayer,’

but you have made it a ‘den of robbers’!”
verses.47: He was teaching daily in the temple, but the chief priests and the scribes and the leading men among the people sought to destroy him.
verses.48: They couldn’t find what they might do, for all the people hung on to every word that he said.

verses.1:
On one of those days, as he was teaching the people in the temple and preaching the Good News, the
priests and scribes came to him with the elders.
verses.2: They asked him, “Tell us: by what authority do you do these things? Or who is giving you this authority?”
verses.3:
He answered them,
“I also will ask you one question. Tell me:
verses.4: the baptism of John, was it from heaven, or from men?”
verses.5: They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why didn’t you believe him?’
verses.6: But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are persuaded that John was a prophet.”
verses.7: They answered that they didn’t know where it was from.
verses.8:
Jesus said to them,
“Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
verses.9:
He began to tell the people this parable.
“A

man planted a vineyard, and rented it out to some farmers, and went into another country for a long time.
verses.10: At the proper season, he sent a servant to the farmers to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the farmers beat him, and sent him away empty.
verses.11: He sent yet another servant, and they also beat him, and treated him shamefully, and sent him away empty.
verses.12: He sent yet a third, and they also wounded him, and threw him out.
verses.13: The lord of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son. It may be that seeing him, they will respect him.’
verses.14: “But when the farmers saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.’
verses.15: They threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him. What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do to them?
verses.16:
He will come and destroy these farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.”
When they heard it, they said, “May it never be!”
verses.17:
But he looked at them, and said,
“Then what is this that is written,
‘The stone which the builders rejected,
the same was made the chief cornerstone?’
verses.18:
Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces,

but it will crush whomever it falls on to dust.”
verses.19: The chief priests and the scribes sought to lay hands on him that very hour, but they feared the people—for they knew he had spoken this parable against them.
verses.20: They watched him, and sent out spies, who pretended to be righteous, that they might trap him in something he said, so as to deliver him up to the power and authority of the governor.
verses.21: They asked him, “Teacher, we know that you say and teach what is right, and aren’t partial to anyone, but truly teach the way of God.
verses.22: Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”
verses.23:
But he perceived their craftiness, and said to them,
“Why do you test me?
verses.24:
Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription are on it?”

They answered, “Caesar’s.”
verses.25:
He said to them,
“Then give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
verses.26: They weren’t able to trap him in his words before the people. They marveled at his answer, and were silent.
verses.27: Some of the Sadducees came to him, those who deny that there is a resurrection.
verses.28: They asked him, “Teacher, Moses wrote to us that if a man’s brother dies having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take the wife, and raise up children for his brother.
verses.29: There were therefore seven brothers. The first took a wife, and died childless.
verses.30: The second took her as wife, and he died childless.
verses.31: The third took her, and likewise the seven all left no children, and died.
verses.32: Afterward the woman also died.
verses.33: Therefore in the resurrection whose wife of them will she be? For the seven had her as a wife.”
verses.34:
Jesus said to them,
“The children of this age marry, and are given in marriage.
verses.35: But those who are considered worthy to attain to that age and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage.
verses.36: For they can’t die any more, for they are like the angels, and are children of God, being children of the resurrection.
verses.37: But that the dead are raised, even Moses showed at the bush, when he called the Lord ‘The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’
verses.38: Now he is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for all are alive to him.”
verses.39: Some of the scribes answered, “Teacher, you speak well.”
verses.40: They didn’t dare to ask him any more questions.
verses.41:
He said to them,
“Why do they say that the Christ is David’s son?
verses.42:
David himself says in the book of Psalms,
‘The Lord said to my Lord,
“Sit at my right hand,
verses.43: until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.”’
verses.44: “David therefore calls him Lord, so how is he his son?”
verses.45: In the hearing of all the people, he said to his disciples,
verses.46: “Beware of those scribes who like to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the marketplaces, the best seats in the synagogues, and the best places at feasts;
verses.47: who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers: these will receive greater condemnation.”

verses.1: He looked up, and saw the rich people who were putting their gifts into the treasury.
verses.2: He saw a certain poor widow casting in two small brass coins.
verses.3:
He said,
“Truly I tell you, this poor widow put in more than all of them,
verses.4: for all these put in gifts for God from their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in all that she had to live on.”
verses.5: As some were talking about the temple and how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts, he said,
verses.6: “As for these things which you see, the days will come, in which there will not be left here one stone on another that will not be thrown down.”
verses.7: They asked him, “Teacher, so when will these things be? What is the sign that these things are about to happen?”
verses.8:
He said,
“Watch out that you don’t get led astray, for many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time is at hand.’ Therefore don’t follow them.
verses.9: When you hear of wars and disturbances, don’t be terrified, for these things must happen first, but the end won’t come immediately.”
verses.10:
Then he said to them,
“Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
verses.11: There will be great earthquakes, famines, and plagues in various places. There will be terrors and great signs from heaven.
verses.12: But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you and will persecute you, delivering you up to synagogues and prisons, bringing you before kings and governors for my name’s sake.
verses.13: It will turn out as a testimony for you.
verses.14: Settle it therefore in your hearts not to meditate beforehand how to answer,
verses.15: for I will give you a mouth and wisdom which all your adversaries will not be able to withstand or to contradict.
verses.16: You will be handed over even by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends. They will cause some of you to be put to death.
verses.17: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake.
verses.18: And not a hair of your head will perish.
verses.19: “By your endurance you will win your lives.
verses.20: “But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is at hand.
verses.21: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains. Let those who are in the middle of her depart. Let those who are in the country not enter therein.
verses.22: For these are days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
verses.23: Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who nurse infants in those days! For there will be great distress in the land, and wrath to this people.
verses.24: They will fall by the edge of the sword, and will be led captive into all the nations. Jerusalem will be trampled down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
verses.25: There will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars; and on the earth anxiety of nations, in perplexity for the roaring of the sea and the waves;
verses.26: men fainting for fear, and for expectation of the things which are coming on the world: for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
verses.27: Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
verses.28: But when these things begin to happen, look up, and lift up your heads, because your redemption is near.”
verses.29:
He told them a parable.
“See the fig tree, and all the trees.
verses.30: When they are already budding, you see it and know by your own selves that the summer is already near.
verses.31: Even so you also, when you see these things happening, know that God’s Kingdom is near.
verses.32: Most certainly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all things are accomplished.
verses.33: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will by no means pass away.
verses.34: “So be careful, or your hearts will be loaded down with carousing, drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day will come on you suddenly.
verses.35: For it will come like a snare on all those who dwell on the surface of all the earth.
verses.36: Therefore be watchful all the time, praying that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things that will happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.”
verses.37: Every day Jesus was teaching in the temple, and every night he would go out and spend the night on the mountain that is called Olivet.
verses.38: All the people came early in the morning to him in the temple to hear him.

verses.1: Now the feast of unleavened bread, which is called the Passover, was approaching.
verses.2: The chief priests and the scribes sought how they might put him to death, for they feared the people.
verses.3: Satan entered into Judas, who was also called Iscariot, who was counted with the twelve.
verses.4: He went away, and talked with the chief priests and captains about how he might deliver him to them.
verses.5: They were glad, and agreed to give him money.
verses.6: He consented, and sought an opportunity to deliver him to them in the absence of the multitude.
verses.7: The day of unleavened bread came, on which the Passover must be sacrificed.
verses.8:
Jesus sent Peter and John, saying,
“Go and prepare the Passover for us, that we may eat.”
verses.9: They said to him, “Where do you want us to prepare?”
verses.10:
He said to them,
“Behold, when you have entered into the city, a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him into the house which he enters.
verses.11: Tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’
verses.12: He will show you a large, furnished upper room. Make preparations there.”
verses.13: They went, found things as Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
verses.14: When the hour had come, he sat down with the twelve apostles.
verses.15:
He said to them,
“I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer,
verses.16: for I tell you, I will no longer by any means eat of it until it is fulfilled in God’s Kingdom.”
verses.17:
He received a cup, and when he had given thanks, he said,
“Take this, and share it among yourselves,
verses.18: for I tell you, I will not drink at all again from the fruit of the vine, until God’s Kingdom comes.”
verses.19:
He took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke, and gave it to them, saying,
“This is my body which is given for you. Do this in memory of me.”
verses.20:
Likewise, he took the cup after supper, saying,
“This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.
verses.21: But behold, the hand of him who betrays me is with me on the table.
verses.22: The Son of Man indeed goes, as it has been determined, but woe to that man through whom he is betrayed!”
verses.23: They began to question among themselves, which of them it was who would do this thing.
verses.24: There arose also a contention among them, which of them was considered to be greatest.
verses.25:
He said to them,
“The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who have authority over them are called ‘benefactors.’
verses.26: But not so with you. But one who is the greater among you, let him become as the younger, and one who is governing, as one who serves.
verses.27: For who is greater, one who sits at the table, or one who serves? Isn’t it he who sits at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.
verses.28: But you are those who have continued with me in my trials.
verses.29: I confer on you a kingdom, even as my Father conferred on me,
verses.30: that you may eat and drink at my table in my Kingdom. You will sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”
verses.31:
The Lord said,
“Simon, Simon, behold, Satan asked to have all of you, that he might sift you as wheat,
verses.32: but I prayed for you, that your faith wouldn’t fail. You, when once you have turned again, establish your brothers.”
verses.33: He said to him, “Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death!”
verses.34:
He said,
“I tell you, Peter, the rooster will by no means crow today until you deny that you know me three times.”
verses.35:
He said to them,
“When I sent you out without purse, and wallet, and shoes, did you lack anything?”
They said, “Nothing.”
verses.36:
Then he said to them,
“But now, whoever has a purse, let him take it, and likewise a wallet. Whoever has none, let him sell his cloak, and buy a sword.
verses.37:
For I tell you that this which is written must still be fulfilled in me: ‘He was counted with transgressors.’
For that which concerns me has an end.”
verses.38:
They said, “Lord, behold, here are two swords.”
He said to them,
“That is enough.”
verses.39: He came out, and went, as his custom was, to the Mount of Olives. His disciples also followed him.
verses.40:
When he was at the place, he said to them,
“Pray that you don’t enter into temptation.”
verses.41: He was withdrawn from them about a stone’s throw, and he knelt down and prayed,
verses.42:
saying,
“Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”
verses.43: An angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.
verses.44: Being in agony he prayed more earnestly. His sweat became like great drops of blood falling down on the ground.
verses.45: When he rose up from his prayer, he came to the disciples, and found them sleeping because of grief,
verses.46:
and said to them,
“Why do you sleep? Rise and pray that you may not enter into temptation.”
verses.47: While he was still speaking, behold, a multitude, and he who was called Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them. He came near to Jesus to kiss him.
verses.48:
But Jesus said to him,
“Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?”
verses.49: When those who were around him saw what was about to happen, they said to him, “Lord, shall we strike with the sword?”
verses.50: A certain one of them struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear.
verses.51:
But Jesus answered,
“Let me at least do this”—and he touched his ear, and healed him.
verses.52:
Jesus said to the chief priests, captains of the temple, and elders, who had come against him,
“Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?
verses.53: When I was with you in the temple daily, you didn’t stretch out your hands against me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness.”
verses.54: They seized him, and led him away, and brought him into the high priest’s house. But Peter followed from a distance.
verses.55: When they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard, and had sat down together, Peter sat among them.
verses.56: A certain servant girl saw him as he sat in the light, and looking intently at him, said, “This man also was with him.”
verses.57: He denied Jesus, saying, “Woman, I don’t know him.”
verses.58:
After a little while someone else saw him, and said, “You also are one of them!”
But Peter answered, “Man, I am not!”
verses.59: After about one hour passed, another confidently affirmed, saying, “Truly this man also was with him, for he is a Galilean!”
verses.60: But Peter said, “Man, I don’t know what you are talking about!” Immediately, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
verses.61:
The Lord turned, and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the Lord’s word, how he said to him,
“Before the rooster crows you will deny me three times.”
verses.62: He went out, and wept bitterly.
verses.63: The men who held Jesus mocked him and beat him.
verses.64: Having blindfolded him, they struck him on the face and asked him, “Prophesy! Who is the one who struck you?”
verses.65: They spoke many other things against him, insulting him.
verses.66: As soon as it was day, the assembly of the elders of the people were gathered together, both chief priests and scribes, and they led him away into their council, saying,
verses.67:
“If you are the Christ, tell us.”
But he said to them,
“If I tell you, you won’t believe,
verses.68: and if I ask, you will in no way answer me or let me go.
verses.69: From now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
verses.70:
They all said, “Are you then the Son of God?”
He said to them,
“You say it, because I am.”
verses.71: They said, “Why do we need any more witness? For we ourselves have heard from his own mouth!”

verses.1: Follow after love, and earnestly desire spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy.
verses.2: For he who speaks in another language speaks not to men, but to God; for no one understands; but in the Spirit he speaks mysteries.
verses.3: But he who prophesies speaks to men for their edification, exhortation, and consolation.
verses.4: He who speaks in another language edifies himself, but he who prophesies edifies the assembly.
verses.5: Now I desire to have you all speak with other languages, but rather that you would prophesy. For he is greater who prophesies than he who speaks with other languages, unless he interprets, that the assembly may be built up.
verses.6: But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking with other languages, what would I profit you, unless I speak to you either by way of revelation, or of knowledge, or of prophesying, or of teaching?
verses.7: Even things without life, giving a voice, whether pipe or harp, if they didn’t give a distinction in the sounds, how would it be known what is piped or harped?
verses.8: For if the trumpet gave an uncertain sound, who would prepare himself for war?
verses.9: So also you, unless you uttered by the tongue words easy to understand, how would it be known what is spoken? For you would be speaking into the air.
verses.10: There are, it may be, so many kinds of sounds in the world, and none of them is without meaning.
verses.11: If then I don’t know the meaning of the sound, I would be to him who speaks a foreigner, and he who speaks would be a foreigner to me.
verses.12: So also you, since you are zealous for spiritual gifts, seek that you may abound to the building up of the assembly.
verses.13: Therefore let him who speaks in another language pray that he may interpret.
verses.14: For if I pray in another language, my spirit prays, but my understanding is unfruitful.
verses.15: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also. I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.
verses.16: Otherwise if you bless with the spirit, how will he who fills the place of the unlearned say the “Amen” at your giving of thanks, seeing he doesn’t know what you say?
verses.17: For you most certainly give thanks well, but the other person is not built up.
verses.18: I thank my God, I speak with other languages more than you all.
verses.19: However in the assembly I would rather speak five words with my understanding, that I might instruct others also, than ten thousand words in another language.
verses.20: Brothers, don’t be children in thoughts, yet in malice be babies, but in thoughts be mature.
verses.21: In the law it is written, “By men of strange languages and by the lips of strangers I will speak to this people. Not even thus will they hear me, says the Lord.”
verses.22: Therefore other languages are for a sign, not to those who believe, but to the unbelieving; but prophesying is for a sign, not to the unbelieving, but to those who believe.
verses.23: If therefore the whole assembly is assembled together and all speak with other languages, and unlearned or unbelieving people come in, won’t they say that you are crazy?
verses.24: But if all prophesy, and someone unbelieving or unlearned comes in, he is reproved by all, and he is judged by all.
verses.25: And thus the secrets of his heart are revealed. So he will fall down on his face and worship God, declaring that God is among you indeed.
verses.26: What is it then, brothers? When you come together, each one of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has another language, has an interpretation. Let all things be done to build each other up.
verses.27: If any man speaks in another language, let it be two, or at the most three, and in turn; and let one interpret.
verses.28: But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in the assembly, and let him speak to himself, and to God.
verses.29: Let the prophets speak, two or three, and let the others discern.
verses.30: But if a revelation is made to another sitting by, let the first keep silent.
verses.31: For you all can prophesy one by one, that all may learn, and all may be exhorted.
verses.32: The spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets,
verses.33: for God is not a God of confusion, but of peace, as in all the assemblies of the saints.
verses.34: Let the wives be quiet in the assemblies, for it has not been permitted for them to be talking except in submission, as the law also says,
verses.35: if they desire to learn anything. “Let them ask their own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a wife to be talking in the assembly.”
verses.36: What!? Was it from you that the word of God went out? Or did it come to you alone?
verses.37: If any man thinks himself to be a prophet, or spiritual, let him recognize the things which I write to you, that they are the commandment of the Lord.
verses.38: But if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant.
verses.39: Therefore, brothers, desire earnestly to prophesy, and don’t forbid speaking with other languages.
verses.40: Let all things be done decently and in order.

verses.1: Now I declare to you, brothers, the Good News which I preached to you, which also you received, in which you also stand,
verses.2: by which also you are saved, if you hold firmly the word which I preached to you—unless you believed in vain.
verses.3: For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
verses.4: that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
verses.5: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.
verses.6: Then he appeared to over five hundred brothers at once, most of whom remain until now, but some have also fallen asleep.
verses.7: Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles,
verses.8: and last of all, as to the child born at the wrong time, he appeared to me also.
verses.9: For I am the least of the apostles, who is not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the assembly of God.
verses.10: But by the grace of God I am what I am. His grace which was given to me was not futile, but I worked more than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.
verses.11: Whether then it is I or they, so we preach, and so you believed.
verses.12: Now if Christ is preached, that he has been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
verses.13: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised.
verses.14: If Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is in vain, and your faith also is in vain.
verses.15: Yes, we are also found false witnesses of God, because we testified about God that he raised up Christ, whom he didn’t raise up, if it is so that the dead are not raised.
verses.16: For if the dead aren’t raised, neither has Christ been raised.
verses.17: If Christ has not been raised, your faith is vain; you are still in your sins.
verses.18: Then they also who are fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
verses.19: If we have only hoped in Christ in this life, we are of all men most pitiable.
verses.20: But now Christ has been raised from the dead. He became the first fruits of those who are asleep.
verses.21: For since death came by man, the resurrection of the dead also came by man.
verses.22: For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.
verses.23: But each in his own order: Christ the first fruits, then those who are Christ’s, at his coming.
verses.24: Then the end comes, when he will deliver up the Kingdom to God, even the Father; when he will have abolished all rule and all authority and power.
verses.25: For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.
verses.26: The last enemy that will be abolished is death.
verses.27: For, “He put all things in subjection under his feet.” But when he says, “All things are put in subjection”, it is evident that he is excepted who subjected all things to him.
verses.28: When all things have been subjected to him, then the Son will also himself be subjected to him who subjected all things to him, that God may be all in all.
verses.29: Or else what will they do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead aren’t raised at all, why then are they baptized for the dead?
verses.30: Why do we also stand in jeopardy every hour?
verses.31: I affirm, by the boasting in you which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.
verses.32: If I fought with animals at Ephesus for human purposes, what does it profit me? If the dead are not raised, then “let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
verses.33: Don’t be deceived! “Evil companionships corrupt good morals.”
verses.34: Wake up righteously, and don’t sin, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.
verses.35: But someone will say, “How are the dead raised?” and, “With what kind of body do they come?”
verses.36: You foolish one, that which you yourself sow is not made alive unless it dies.
verses.37: That which you sow, you don’t sow the body that will be, but a bare grain, maybe of wheat, or of some other kind.
verses.38: But God gives it a body even as it pleased him, and to each seed a body of its own.
verses.39: All flesh is not the same flesh, but there is one flesh of men, another flesh of animals, another of fish, and another of birds.
verses.40: There are also celestial bodies, and terrestrial bodies; but the glory of the celestial differs from that of the terrestrial.
verses.41: There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differs from another star in glory.
verses.42: So also is the resurrection of the dead. The body is sown perishable; it is raised imperishable.
verses.43: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
verses.44: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body and there is also a spiritual body.
verses.45:
So also it is written, “The first man, Adam, became a living soul.”
 The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
verses.46: However that which is spiritual isn’t first, but that which is natural, then that which is spiritual.
verses.47: The first man is of the earth, made of dust. The second man is the Lord from heaven.
verses.48: As is the one made of dust, such are those who are also made of dust; and as is the heavenly, such are they also that are heavenly.
verses.49: As we have borne the image of those made of dust, let’s also bear the image of the heavenly.
verses.50: Now I say this, brothers, that flesh and blood can’t inherit God’s Kingdom; neither does the perishable inherit imperishable.
verses.51: Behold, I tell you a mystery. We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed,
verses.52: in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.
verses.53: For this perishable body must become imperishable, and this mortal must put on immortality.
verses.54: But when this perishable body will have become imperishable, and this mortal will have put on immortality, then what is written will happen: “Death is swallowed up in victory.”
verses.55:
“Death, where is your sting?
Hades, where is your victory?”
verses.56: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
verses.57: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.58: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, because you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.

verses.1: Now concerning the collection for the saints, as I commanded the assemblies of Galatia, you do likewise.
verses.2: On the first day of the week, let each one of you save, as he may prosper, that no collections be made when I come.
verses.3: When I arrive, I will send whoever you approve with letters to carry your gracious gift to Jerusalem.
verses.4: If it is appropriate for me to go also, they will go with me.
verses.5: But I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia.
verses.6: But with you it may be that I will stay, or even winter, that you may send me on my journey wherever I go.
verses.7: For I do not wish to see you now in passing, but I hope to stay a while with you, if the Lord permits.
verses.8: But I will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost,
verses.9: for a great and effective door has opened to me, and there are many adversaries.
verses.10: Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear, for he does the work of the Lord, as I also do.
verses.11: Therefore let no one despise him. But set him forward on his journey in peace, that he may come to me; for I expect him with the brothers.
verses.12: Now concerning Apollos, the brother, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers; and it was not at all his desire to come now; but he will come when he has an opportunity.
verses.13: Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong!
verses.14: Let all that you do be done in love.
verses.15: Now I beg you, brothers (you know the house of Stephanas, that it is the first fruits of Achaia, and that they have set themselves to serve the saints),
verses.16: that you also be in subjection to such, and to everyone who helps in the work and labors.
verses.17: I rejoice at the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus; for that which was lacking on your part, they supplied.
verses.18: For they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore acknowledge those who are like that.
verses.19: The assemblies of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you much in the Lord, together with the assembly that is in their house.
verses.20: All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
verses.21: This greeting is by me, Paul, with my own hand.
verses.22:
If any man doesn’t love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed.
 Come, Lord!
verses.23: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
verses.24: My love to all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

verses.1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother, to the assembly of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints who are in the whole of Achaia:
verses.2: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort;
verses.4: who comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
verses.5: For as the sufferings of Christ abound to us, even so our comfort also abounds through Christ.
verses.6: But if we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation. If we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which produces in you the patient enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer.
verses.7: Our hope for you is steadfast, knowing that, since you are partakers of the sufferings, so also are you of the comfort.
verses.8: For we don’t desire to have you uninformed, brothers, concerning our affliction which happened to us in Asia, that we were weighed down exceedingly, beyond our power, so much that we despaired even of life.
verses.9: Yes, we ourselves have had the sentence of death within ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead,
verses.10: who delivered us out of so great a death, and does deliver; on whom we have set our hope that he will also still deliver us;
verses.11: you also helping together on our behalf by your supplication; that, for the gift given to us by means of many, thanks may be given by many persons on your behalf.
verses.12: For our boasting is this: the testimony of our conscience, that in holiness and sincerity of God, not in fleshly wisdom but in the grace of God we behaved ourselves in the world, and more abundantly toward you.
verses.13: For we write no other things to you, than what you read or even acknowledge, and I hope you will acknowledge to the end;
verses.14: as also you acknowledged us in part, that we are your boasting, even as you also are ours, in the day of our Lord Jesus.
verses.15: In this confidence, I was determined to come first to you, that you might have a second benefit;
verses.16: and by you to pass into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you, and to be sent forward by you on my journey to Judea.
verses.17: When I therefore was thus determined, did I show fickleness? Or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, that with me there should be the “Yes, yes” and the “No, no?”
verses.18: But as God is faithful, our word toward you was not “Yes and no.”
verses.19: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, by me, Silvanus, and Timothy, was not “Yes and no,” but in him is “Yes.”
verses.20: For however many are the promises of God, in him is the “Yes.” Therefore also through him is the “Amen”, to the glory of God through us.
verses.21: Now he who establishes us with you in Christ, and anointed us, is God;
verses.22: who also sealed us, and gave us the down payment of the Spirit in our hearts.
verses.23: But I call God for a witness to my soul, that I didn’t come to Corinth to spare you.
verses.24: Not that we control your faith, but are fellow workers with you for your joy. For you stand firm in faith.

verses.1: But I determined this for myself, that I would not come to you again in sorrow.
verses.2: For if I make you sorry, then who will make me glad but he who is made sorry by me?
verses.3: And I wrote this very thing to you, so that, when I came, I wouldn’t have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice; having confidence in you all, that my joy would be shared by all of you.
verses.4: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears, not that you should be made sorry, but that you might know the love that I have so abundantly for you.
verses.5: But if any has caused sorrow, he has caused sorrow, not to me, but in part (that I not press too heavily) to you all.
verses.6: This punishment which was inflicted by the many is sufficient for such a one;
verses.7: so that on the contrary you should rather forgive him and comfort him, lest by any means such a one should be swallowed up with his excessive sorrow.
verses.8: Therefore I beg you to confirm your love toward him.
verses.9: For to this end I also wrote, that I might know the proof of you, whether you are obedient in all things.
verses.10: Now I also forgive whomever you forgive anything. For if indeed I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven that one for your sakes in the presence of Christ,
verses.11: that no advantage may be gained over us by Satan; for we are not ignorant of his schemes.
verses.12: Now when I came to Troas for the Good News of Christ, and when a door was opened to me in the Lord,
verses.13: I had no relief for my spirit, because I didn’t find Titus, my brother, but taking my leave of them, I went out into Macedonia.
verses.14: Now thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumph in Christ, and reveals through us the sweet aroma of his knowledge in every place.
verses.15: For we are a sweet aroma of Christ to God, in those who are saved, and in those who perish;
verses.16: to the one a stench from death to death; to the other a sweet aroma from life to life. Who is sufficient for these things?
verses.17: For we are not as so many, peddling the word of God. But as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God, we speak in Christ.

verses.1: Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? Or do we need, as do some, letters of commendation to you or from you?
verses.2: You are our letter, written in our hearts, known and read by all men;
verses.3: being revealed that you are a letter of Christ, served by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tablets of stone, but in tablets that are hearts of flesh.
verses.4: Such confidence we have through Christ toward God;
verses.5: not that we are sufficient of ourselves, to account anything as from ourselves; but our sufficiency is from God;
verses.6: who also made us sufficient as servants of a new covenant; not of the letter, but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
verses.7: But if the service of death, written engraved on stones, came with glory, so that the children of Israel could not look steadfastly on the face of Moses for the glory of his face, which was passing away;
verses.8: won’t service of the Spirit be with much more glory?
verses.9: For if the service of condemnation has glory, the service of righteousness exceeds much more in glory.
verses.10: For most certainly that which has been made glorious has not been made glorious in this respect, by reason of the glory that surpasses.
verses.11: For if that which passes away was with glory, much more that which remains is in glory.
verses.12: Having therefore such a hope, we use great boldness of speech,
verses.13: and not as Moses, who put a veil on his face, that the children of Israel wouldn’t look steadfastly on the end of that which was passing away.
verses.14: But their minds were hardened, for until this very day at the reading of the old covenant the same veil remains, because in Christ it passes away.
verses.15: But to this day, when Moses is read, a veil lies on their heart.
verses.16: But whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
verses.17: Now the Lord is the Spirit and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.
verses.18: But we all, with unveiled face seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord, the Spirit.

verses.1: Therefore seeing we have this ministry, even as we obtained mercy, we don’t faint.
verses.2: But we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.
verses.3: Even if our Good News is veiled, it is veiled in those who are dying;
verses.4: in whom the god of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelieving, that the light of the Good News of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should not dawn on them.
verses.5: For we don’t preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake;
verses.6: seeing it is God who said, “Light will shine out of darkness,” who has shone in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
verses.7: But we have this treasure in clay vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God, and not from ourselves.
verses.8: We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair;
verses.9: pursued, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed;
verses.10: always carrying in the body the putting to death of the Lord Jesus, that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
verses.11: For we who live are always delivered to death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus may be revealed in our mortal flesh.
verses.12: So then death works in us, but life in you.
verses.13: But having the same spirit of faith, according to that which is written, “I believed, and therefore I spoke.” We also believe, and therefore also we speak;
verses.14: knowing that he who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also with Jesus, and will present us with you.
verses.15: For all things are for your sakes, that the grace, being multiplied through the many, may cause the thanksgiving to abound to the glory of God.
verses.16: Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day.
verses.17: For our light affliction, which is for the moment, works for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory;
verses.18: while we don’t look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.

verses.1: For we know that if the earthly house of our tent is dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal, in the heavens.
verses.2: For most certainly in this we groan, longing to be clothed with our habitation which is from heaven;
verses.3: if so be that being clothed we will not be found naked.
verses.4: For indeed we who are in this tent do groan, being burdened; not that we desire to be unclothed, but that we desire to be clothed, that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
verses.5: Now he who made us for this very thing is God, who also gave to us the down payment of the Spirit.
verses.6: Therefore we are always confident and know that while we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord;
verses.7: for we walk by faith, not by sight.
verses.8: We are courageous, I say, and are willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be at home with the Lord.
verses.9: Therefore also we make it our aim, whether at home or absent, to be well pleasing to him.
verses.10: For we must all be revealed before the judgment seat of Christ; that each one may receive the things in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad.
verses.11: Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we persuade men, but we are revealed to God; and I hope that we are revealed also in your consciences.
verses.12: For we are not commending ourselves to you again, but speak as giving you occasion of boasting on our behalf, that you may have something to answer those who boast in appearance, and not in heart.
verses.13: For if we are beside ourselves, it is for God. Or if we are of sober mind, it is for you.
verses.14: For the love of Christ constrains us; because we judge thus, that one died for all, therefore all died.
verses.15: He died for all, that those who live should no longer live to themselves, but to him who for their sakes died and rose again.
verses.16: Therefore we know no one after the flesh from now on. Even though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now we know him so no more.
verses.17: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
verses.18: But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave to us the ministry of reconciliation;
verses.19: namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning to them their trespasses, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.
verses.20: We are therefore ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beg you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.
verses.21: For him who knew no sin he made to be sin on our behalf; so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

verses.1: Working together, we entreat also that you do not receive the grace of God in vain,
verses.2:
for he says,
“At an acceptable time I listened to you,
in a day of salvation I helped you.”
Behold, now is the acceptable time. Behold, now is the day of salvation.
verses.3: We give no occasion of stumbling in anything, that our service may not be blamed,
verses.4: but in everything commending ourselves, as servants of God, in great endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in distresses,
verses.5: in beatings, in imprisonments, in riots, in labors, in watchings, in fastings;
verses.6: in pureness, in knowledge, in perseverance, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in sincere love,
verses.7: in the word of truth, in the power of God; by the armor of righteousness on the right hand and on the left,
verses.8: by glory and dishonor, by evil report and good report; as deceivers, and yet true;
verses.9: as unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and behold, we live; as punished, and not killed;
verses.10: as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things.
verses.11: Our mouth is open to you, Corinthians. Our heart is enlarged.
verses.12: You are not restricted by us, but you are restricted by your own affections.
verses.13: Now in return, I speak as to my children, you also open your hearts.
verses.14: Don’t be unequally yoked with unbelievers, for what fellowship have righteousness and iniquity? Or what fellowship has light with darkness?
verses.15: What agreement has Christ with Belial? Or what portion has a believer with an unbeliever?
verses.16: What agreement has a temple of God with idols? For you are a temple of the living God. Even as God said, “I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they will be my people.”
verses.17:
Therefore
“‘Come out from among them,
and be separate,’ says the Lord.
‘Touch no unclean thing.
I will receive you.
verses.18:
I will be to you a Father.
You will be to me sons and daughters,’
says the Lord Almighty.”

verses.1: Having therefore these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
verses.2: Open your hearts to us. We wronged no one. We corrupted no one. We took advantage of no one.
verses.3: I say this not to condemn you, for I have said before, that you are in our hearts to die together and live together.
verses.4: Great is my boldness of speech toward you. Great is my boasting on your behalf. I am filled with comfort. I overflow with joy in all our affliction.
verses.5: For even when we had come into Macedonia, our flesh had no relief, but we were afflicted on every side. Fightings were outside. Fear was inside.
verses.6: Nevertheless, he who comforts the lowly, God, comforted us by the coming of Titus;
verses.7: and not by his coming only, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted in you, while he told us of your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me; so that I rejoiced still more.
verses.8: For though I made you sorry with my letter, I do not regret it, though I did regret it. For I see that my letter made you sorry, though just for a while.
verses.9: I now rejoice, not that you were made sorry, but that you were made sorry to repentance. For you were made sorry in a godly way, that you might suffer loss by us in nothing.
verses.10: For godly sorrow produces repentance to salvation, which brings no regret. But the sorrow of the world produces death.
verses.11: For behold, this same thing, that you were made sorry in a godly way, what earnest care it worked in you. Yes, what defense, indignation, fear, longing, zeal, and vengeance! In everything you demonstrated yourselves to be pure in the matter.
verses.12: So although I wrote to you, I wrote not for his cause that did the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered the wrong, but that your earnest care for us might be revealed in you in the sight of God.
verses.13: Therefore we have been comforted. In our comfort we rejoiced the more exceedingly for the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by you all.
verses.14: For if in anything I have boasted to him on your behalf, I was not disappointed. But as we spoke all things to you in truth, so our glorying also which I made before Titus was found to be truth.
verses.15: His affection is more abundantly toward you, while he remembers all of your obedience, how with fear and trembling you received him.
verses.16: I rejoice that in everything I am confident concerning you.

verses.1: Moreover, brothers, we make known to you the grace of God which has been given in the assemblies of Macedonia;
verses.2: how that in much proof of affliction the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded to the riches of their generosity.
verses.3: For according to their power, I testify, yes and beyond their power, they gave of their own accord,
verses.4: begging us with much entreaty to receive this grace and the fellowship in the service to the saints.
verses.5: This was not as we had expected, but first they gave their own selves to the Lord, and to us through the will of God.
verses.6: So we urged Titus, that as he had made a beginning before, so he would also complete in you this grace.
verses.7: But as you abound in everything, in faith, utterance, knowledge, all earnestness, and in your love to us, see that you also abound in this grace.
verses.8: I speak not by way of commandment, but as proving through the earnestness of others the sincerity also of your love.
verses.9: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that you through his poverty might become rich.
verses.10: I give a judgment in this: for this is expedient for you, who were the first to start a year ago, not only to do, but also to be willing.
verses.11: But now complete the doing also, that as there was the readiness to be willing, so there may be the completion also out of your ability.
verses.12: For if the readiness is there, it is acceptable according to what you have, not according to what you don’t have.
verses.13: For this is not that others may be eased and you distressed,
verses.14: but for equality. Your abundance at this present time supplies their lack, that their abundance also may become a supply for your lack; that there may be equality.
verses.15: As it is written, “He who gathered much had nothing left over, and he who gathered little had no lack.”
verses.16: But thanks be to God, who puts the same earnest care for you into the heart of Titus.
verses.17: For he indeed accepted our exhortation, but being himself very earnest, he went out to you of his own accord.
verses.18: We have sent together with him the brother whose praise in the Good News is known throughout all the assemblies.
verses.19: Not only so, but he was also appointed by the assemblies to travel with us in this grace, which is served by us to the glory of the Lord himself, and to show our readiness.
verses.20: We are avoiding this, that any man should blame us concerning this abundance which is administered by us.
verses.21: Having regard for honorable things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.
verses.22: We have sent with them our brother, whom we have many times proved earnest in many things, but now much more earnest, by reason of the great confidence which he has in you.
verses.23: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker for you. As for our brothers, they are the apostles of the assemblies, the glory of Christ.
verses.24: Therefore show the proof of your love to them before the assemblies, and of our boasting on your behalf.

verses.1: It is indeed unnecessary for me to write to you concerning the service to the saints,
verses.2: for I know your readiness, of which I boast on your behalf to them of Macedonia, that Achaia has been prepared for a year past. Your zeal has stirred up very many of them.
verses.3: But I have sent the brothers that our boasting on your behalf may not be in vain in this respect, that, just as I said, you may be prepared,
verses.4: lest by any means, if anyone from Macedonia comes there with me and finds you unprepared, we (to say nothing of you) would be disappointed in this confident boasting.
verses.5: I thought it necessary therefore to entreat the brothers that they would go before to you, and arrange ahead of time the generous gift that you promised before, that the same might be ready as a matter of generosity, and not of greediness.
verses.6: Remember this: he who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly. He who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.
verses.7: Let each man give according as he has determined in his heart; not grudgingly, or under compulsion; for God loves a cheerful giver.
verses.8: And God is able to make all grace abound to you, that you, always having all sufficiency in everything, may abound to every good work.
verses.9:
As it is written,
“He has scattered abroad, he has given to the poor.
His righteousness remains forever.”
verses.10: Now may he who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food, supply and multiply your seed for sowing, and increase the fruits of your righteousness;
verses.11: you being enriched in everything to all generosity, which produces through us thanksgiving to God.
verses.12: For this service of giving that you perform not only makes up for lack among the saints, but abounds also through much giving of thanks to God;
